bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第059卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 59.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 59.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀五十一】起著雍執徐，盡上章敦牂，凡三年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 51】 Beginning from Zhuyong Zhixu through Shangzhang Dunzang—in all, three years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 51】 From the year Zhuyong Zhixu through Shangzhang Dunzang—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day dingyou, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dingyou day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，有星孛於紫宮，黃巾餘賊郭大等起於河西白波谷，寇太原、河東。

translations.literal: In the second month, a broom star appeared in the Purple Palace; remnant Yellow Turban bandits Guo Da and others rose in the White Wave Valley of Hexi and raided Taiyuan and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month a comet appeared in the Purple Palace constellation, and remnant Yellow Turban rebels led by Guo Da rose in the White Wave Valley of Hexi and attacked Taiyuan and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 三月，屠各胡攻殺并州刺史張懿。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Tuge Hu attacked and killed the Inspector of Bing Province, Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Tuge Xiongnu attacked and killed Zhang Yi, inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 太常江夏劉焉見王室多故，建議以為：「四方兵寇，由刺史威輕，既不能禁，且用非其人，以致離叛。

translations.literal: The Grand Minister of Ceremonies Liu Yan of Jiangxia, seeing that the royal house had many troubles, submitted a proposal saying: "Banditry in the four quarters stems from the governors' authority being too light—they can neither suppress it, and moreover unfit men are appointed, leading to defection and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan of Jiangxia, grand minister of ceremonies, seeing how troubled the imperial house had become, proposed: "Rebellion on every side arises because provincial inspectors lack sufficient authority—they cannot suppress disorder, and unworthy men are appointed to office, which drives people to revolt.

sentences.zh: 宜改置牧伯，選清名重臣以居其任。

translations.literal: It is fitting to replace them with regional lords, selecting men of pure reputation and high standing to fill these posts.
translations.idiomatic: The offices should be changed to regional governorships, and men of sterling reputation and high rank should be chosen to hold them.

sentences.zh: 」焉內欲求交趾牧。

translations.literal: " In his heart Yan sought the governorship of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Privately, Yan hoped to be named governor of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 侍中廣漢董扶私謂焉曰：「京師將亂，益州分野有天子氣。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Dong Fu of Guanghan said privately to Yan: "The capital is about to fall into chaos; in the astral domain of Yizhou there is the aura of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant Dong Fu of Guanghan told Yan in private: "The capital is heading for chaos, and the astral domain of Yizhou bears the aura of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 」焉乃更求益州。

translations.literal: " Yan thereupon sought Yizhou instead.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan then asked for Yizhou instead.

sentences.zh: 會益州刺史郤儉賦斂煩擾，謠言遠聞，而耿鄙、張懿皆為盜所殺，朝廷遂從焉議，選列卿、尚書為州牧，各以本秩居任。

translations.literal: It happened that the Inspector of Yizhou, Xi Jian, levied taxes in a vexatious and oppressive manner, and rumors of this spread far; moreover Geng Bi and Zhang Yi had both been killed by bandits. The court thereupon adopted Yan's proposal, selecting chief ministers and imperial secretaries as regional governors, each holding office at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Yizhou inspector Xi Jian was taxing the people harshly, and word of his abuses spread widely; Geng Bi and Zhang Yi had also been killed by bandits. The court accepted Yan's plan and appointed chief ministers and imperial secretaries as regional governors, each serving at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 以焉為益州牧，太僕黃琬為豫州牧，宗正東海劉虞為幽州牧。

translations.literal: Yan was made Governor of Yizhou, Huang Wan the Grand Coachman was made Governor of Yuzhou, and Liu Yu of Donghai, Director of the Imperial Clan, was made Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was named governor of Yizhou, Huang Wan grand coachman was named governor of Yuzhou, and Liu Yu of Donghai, director of the imperial clan, was named governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 州任之重，自此而始。

translations.literal: The weight of provincial responsibility began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the governorships of the provinces took on their full weight of authority.

sentences.zh: 焉，魯恭王之後；

translations.literal: Yan was a descendant of King Gong of Lu;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was a descendant of King Gong of Lu;

sentences.zh: 虞，東海恭王之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Yu was a fifth-generation descendant of King Gong of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was a fifth-generation descendant of King Gong of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 虞嘗為幽州刺史，民夷懷其恩信，故用之。

translations.literal: Yu had once served as Inspector of You Province; the people and the barbarians cherished his kindness and trustworthiness, and so he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had once been inspector of You Province, and both Han and non-Han peoples there cherished his kindness and integrity, which was why he was chosen.

sentences.zh: 董扶及太倉令趙韙皆棄官，隨焉入蜀。

translations.literal: Dong Fu and Zhao Wei, Director of the Imperial Granary, both resigned their offices and followed Yan into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fu and Zhao Wei, director of the imperial granary, both resigned their posts and accompanied Yan into Shu.

sentences.zh: 詔發南匈奴兵配劉虞討張純，單于羌渠遣左賢王將騎詣幽州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the mobilization of Southern Xiongnu troops to assist Liu Yu in campaigning against Zhang Chun; the Chanyu Qiangqu sent the Left Worthy King to lead cavalry to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Southern Xiongnu forces sent to aid Liu Yu against Zhang Chun; Chanyu Qiangqu dispatched the Left Worthy King with cavalry to You Province.

sentences.zh: 國人恐發兵無已，於是右部□盆落反，與屠各胡合，凡十餘萬人，攻殺羌渠。

translations.literal: The tribesmen feared that troop levies would never cease; thereupon the right wing □ Penluo rebelled, joined with the Tuge Hu, and in all more than a hundred thousand men attacked and killed Qiangqu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu feared endless levies of troops; chiefs of the right wing under Penluo then rebelled, joined the Tuge Xiongnu, and with more than a hundred thousand men attacked and killed Qiangqu.

sentences.zh: 國人立其子右賢王於扶羅為持至屍逐侯單于。

translations.literal: The tribesmen enthroned his son, the Right Worthy King Yufoluo, as Chanyu Chizhi Shizhu Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu enthroned his son, the Right Worthy King Yufoluo, as Chanyu Chizhi Shizhu.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，太尉曹嵩罷。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Grand Commandant Cao Song was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Grand Commandant Cao Song was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 五月，以永樂少府南陽樊陵為太尉；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Fan Ling of Nanyang, Junior Chamberlain of Yongle, was appointed Grand Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Fan Ling of Nanyang, junior chamberlain of Yongle, was appointed grand commandant;

sentences.zh: 六月，罷。

translations.literal: in the sixth month he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: and in the sixth month he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 益州賊馬相、趙祗等起兵綿竹，自號黃巾，殺刺史郤儉，進擊巴郡、犍為，旬月之間，破壞三郡，有眾數萬，相自稱天子。

translations.literal: In Yizhou the bandits Ma Xiang, Zhao Di, and others raised troops at Mianzhu, styled themselves Yellow Turbans, killed the Inspector Xi Jian, and advanced to attack Ba Commandery and Jianwei; within a month or so they ravaged three commanderies, gathered a force of tens of thousands, and Xiang proclaimed himself Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Yizhou the rebels Ma Xiang, Zhao Di, and others rose at Mianzhu, called themselves Yellow Turbans, killed Inspector Xi Jian, and attacked Ba and Jianwei commanderies; within a month they had laid waste to three commanderies and gathered tens of thousands of followers, and Ma Xiang declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 州從事賈龍率吏民攻相等，數日破走，州界清靜。

translations.literal: The provincial aide Jia Long led officials and commoners to attack Xiang and the others; within several days he routed them, and the province was restored to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial aide Jia Long led officials and people against Ma Xiang and his followers; within days he drove them off, and the province was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 龍乃選吏卒迎劉焉。

translations.literal: Long then selected officials and soldiers to welcome Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Long then chose officials and troops to escort Liu Yan into the province.

sentences.zh: 焉徙治綿竹，撫納離叛，務行寬惠，以收人心。

translations.literal: Yan moved his seat of government to Mianzhu, comforted and received those who had defected, and devoted himself to lenient and generous policies in order to win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan moved his seat to Mianzhu, reassured defectors, and pursued lenient and generous policies to win the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 郡國七大水。

translations.literal: Seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods struck seven commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 故太傅陳蕃子逸與術士襄楷會於冀州刺史王芬坐，楷曰：「天文不利宦者，黃門、常侍真族滅矣。

translations.literal: Chen Yi, son of the former Grand Tutor Chen Fan, met with the occultist Xiang Kai at the seat of Wang Fen, Inspector of Ji Province; Kai said: "The heavens are unfavorable to the eunuchs—the Yellow Gates and Regular Attendants will truly be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi, son of the late Grand Tutor Chen Fan, met the occultist Xiang Kai at a gathering hosted by Ji Province inspector Wang Fen; Kai said, "The heavens are against the eunuchs—the Yellow Gates and Regular Attendants are doomed to extinction.

sentences.zh: 」逸喜。

translations.literal: " Yi was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Yi was delighted.

sentences.zh: 芬曰：「若然者，芬願驅除！

translations.literal: Fen said: "If that is so, Fen is willing to drive them out!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen said, "If that is so, I am ready to drive them out!

sentences.zh: 」因與豪傑轉相招合，上書言黑山賊攻劫郡縣，欲因以起兵。

translations.literal: " He thereupon recruited heroes and worthies in succession, submitted a memorial saying that Black Mountain bandits were attacking and plundering commanderies and counties, and intended to use this as a pretext to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recruited local leaders one after another, memorialized that Black Mountain bandits were raiding commanderies and counties, and planned to use that as a pretext to raise an army.

sentences.zh: 會帝欲北巡河間舊宅，芬等謀以兵徼劫，誅諸常侍、黃門，因廢帝，立合肥侯，以其謀告議郎曹操。

translations.literal: It happened that the Emperor wished to tour north to his old residence in Hejian; Fen and the others plotted to intercept him with troops, execute the Regular Attendants and Yellow Gates, depose the Emperor, and enthrone the Marquis of Hefei, and they disclosed their plot to the Consultant Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a northern tour to his old residence in Hejian, Fen and his allies plotted to ambush him with troops, kill the Regular Attendants and Yellow Gates, depose the emperor, and enthrone the Marquis of Hefei; they confided the plan to Consultant Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「夫廢立之事，天下之至不祥也。

translations.literal: Cao said: "Matters of deposition and enthronement are the greatest ill omen under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Deposing and enthroning rulers is the gravest ill omen in the realm.

sentences.zh: 古人有權成敗、計輕重而行之者，伊、霍是也。

translations.literal: The ancients had those who weighed success and failure and calculated what was light and heavy before acting—Yi Yin and Huo Guang were such men.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who acted only after weighing success against failure and judging what mattered most were men like Yi Yin and Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 伊、霍皆懷至忠之誠，據宰輔之勢，因秉政之重，同眾人之欲，故能計從事立。

translations.literal: Yi and Huo both harbored the utmost loyalty, held the power of chief ministers, leveraged the weight of governing the state, and shared the people's desires—therefore their plans were followed and their aims achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin and Huo Guang were utterly loyal, held the power of chief ministers, commanded the weight of government, and acted with the people's support—only then could their plans succeed.

sentences.zh: 今諸君徒見曩者之易，未睹當今之難，而造作非常，慾望必克，不亦危乎！

translations.literal: Now you gentlemen see only how easy it was in former times and have not perceived how difficult it is today, yet you undertake something extraordinary and expect certain success—is this not perilous!
translations.idiomatic: You see only how easy it seemed in the past and not how hard it is now, yet you attempt something unprecedented and expect certain success—is that not reckless!

sentences.zh: 」芬又呼平原華歆、陶丘洪共定計。

translations.literal: " Fen again summoned Hua Xin of Pingyuan and Taoqiu Hong to settle the plan together.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Fen then called in Hua Xin of Pingyuan and Taoqiu Hong to finalize the plan.

sentences.zh: 洪欲行，歆止之曰：「夫廢立大事，伊、霍之所難。

translations.literal: Hong wished to go, but Xin stopped him and said: "Deposition and enthronement are great affairs—even Yi and Huo found them difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was ready to go, but Xin stopped him and said, "Deposing and enthroning rulers is a grave matter—even Yi Yin and Huo Guang found it hard.

sentences.zh: 芬性疏而不武，此必無成。

translations.literal: Fen's nature is careless and he is not martial—this will certainly fail.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen is careless by nature and no soldier—this cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 」洪乃止。

translations.literal: " Hong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 會北方夜半有赤氣，東西竟天，太史上言：「北方有陰謀，不宜北行。

translations.literal: It happened that at midnight in the north there was a red vapor stretching east and west across the sky; the Grand Astrologer submitted a memorial: "There is a secret plot in the north—it is not fitting to travel north.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a red vapor stretched across the northern sky from east to west; the grand astrologer reported, "There is a conspiracy in the north—the northern tour should not proceed.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor canceled the tour.

sentences.zh: 敕芬罷兵，俄而征之。

translations.literal: He ordered Fen to disband his troops, and shortly afterward summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wang Fen to disband his forces, then soon afterward summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 芬懼，解印綬亡走，至平原，自殺。

translations.literal: Fen was afraid, relinquished his seal and ribbon and fled; when he reached Pingyuan he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen, terrified, surrendered his seal and ribbon and fled; reaching Pingyuan, he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以射聲校尉馬日磾為太尉。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Ma Midi, Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Ma Midi, colonel of the archers who shoot at sound, was appointed grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 日磾，融之族孫也。

translations.literal: Midi was a collateral descendant of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi was a collateral descendant of Ma Rong.

sentences.zh: 八月，初置西園八校尉，以小黃門蹇碩為上軍校尉，虎賁中郎將袁紹為中軍校尉，屯騎校尉鮑鴻為下軍校尉，議郎曹操為典軍校尉，趙融為助軍左校尉，馮芳為助軍右校尉，諫議大夫夏牟為左校尉，淳於瓊為右校尉；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Eight Colonels of the Western Garden were first established: the Junior Yellow Gate Jian Shuo as Colonel of the Upper Army, the Tiger-Fierce Gentlemen-Commandant Yuan Shao as Colonel of the Central Army, the Colonel of the Wardens of the Resolute Cavalry Bao Hong as Colonel of the Lower Army, the Consultant Cao Cao as Colonel of the Standard Army, Zhao Rong as Colonel of the Left Army of the Assistant Force, Feng Fang as Colonel of the Right Army of the Assistant Force, the Grand Master of Remonstrance Xia Mou as Colonel of the Left Army, and Chunyu Qiong as Colonel of the Right Army;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Eight Colonels of the Western Garden were established for the first time: the junior yellow gate Jian Shuo as colonel of the upper army, tiger-fierce gentlemen-commandant Yuan Shao as colonel of the central army, colonel of the wardens of the resolute cavalry Bao Hong as colonel of the lower army, consultant Cao Cao as colonel of the standard army, Zhao Rong as colonel of the left army of the assistant force, Feng Fang as colonel of the right army of the assistant force, grand master of remonstrance Xia Mou as colonel of the left army, and Chunyu Qiong as colonel of the right army;

sentences.zh: 皆統於蹇碩。

translations.literal: all were placed under Jian Shuo's command.
translations.idiomatic: all were placed under Jian Shuo's command.

sentences.zh: 帝自黃巾之起，留心戎事；

translations.literal: Since the rise of the Yellow Turbans the Emperor had paid close attention to military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yellow Turban rebellion the emperor had taken a keen interest in military affairs;

sentences.zh: 碩壯健有武略，帝親任之，雖大將軍亦領屬焉。

translations.literal: Shuo was robust and possessed military stratagems; the Emperor personally relied on him, and even the General-in-Chief was subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shuo was strong and skilled in strategy; the emperor trusted him personally, and even the general-in-chief was placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 九月，司徒許相罷；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Grand Secretary Xu Xiang was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Grand Secretary Xu Xiang was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以司空丁宮為司徒，光祿勳南陽劉弘為司空。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Ding Gong was made Grand Secretary, and Liu Hong of Nanyang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Ding Gong was made grand secretary, and Liu Hong of Nanyang, director of the imperial secretariat, was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 以衛尉條侯董重為票騎將軍。

translations.literal: Dong Chong, Marquis of Tiao and Commandant of the Guards, was appointed General of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chong, marquis of Tiao and commandant of the guards, was appointed general of fast cavalry.

sentences.zh: 重，永樂太后兄子也。

translations.literal: Chong was a nephew of Empress Dowager Yongle's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chong was a nephew of Empress Dowager Yongle's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，青、徐黃巾復起，寇郡縣。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Yellow Turbans in Qing and Xu rose again and raided commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Yellow Turban forces in Qing and Xu provinces rose again and attacked commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 望氣者以為京師當有大兵，兩宮流血。

translations.literal: Those who read the qi of the heavens believed that the capital would see great warfare and bloodshed in both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Omen-readers believed the capital would see great warfare and bloodshed in both palaces.

sentences.zh: 帝欲厭之，乃大發四方兵，講武於平樂觀下，起大壇，上建十二重華蓋，高十丈。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to avert this; he therefore mobilized troops from the four quarters on a grand scale and held a military review below the Pingle Observatory, erecting a great altar with a twelve-tiered canopy ten zhang high upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hoped to avert the omen, so he mobilized troops from all directions and held a grand military review below the Pingle Observatory, building a great altar topped with a twelve-tiered canopy ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 壇東北為小壇，復建九重華蓋，高九丈。

translations.literal: To the northeast of the altar a smaller altar was built, with a nine-tiered canopy nine zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast of the main altar a smaller one was built, topped with a nine-tiered canopy nine zhang high.

sentences.zh: 列步騎數萬人，結營為陳。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry were arrayed, encamped in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry were drawn up in encampments forming a battle array.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝親出臨軍，駐大華蓋下，大將軍進駐小華蓋下。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi the Emperor personally came forth to inspect the army, taking his station beneath the great canopy; the General-in-Chief advanced to take his station beneath the small canopy.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the emperor came in person to review the troops, taking his place beneath the great canopy while the general-in-chief took his place beneath the smaller one.

sentences.zh: 帝躬擐甲、介馬，稱「無上將軍」，行陳三匝而還，以兵授進。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself donned armor and barded his horse, styled himself "Supreme General," marched three circuits through the formation and returned, and handed the troops over to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself donned armor and barded his horse, styled himself "Supreme General," rode three circuits through the formation, and then returned and transferred command of the troops to He Jin.

sentences.zh: 帝問討虜校尉蓋勳曰：「吾講武如是，何如？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the Colonel Who Punishes the Barbarians Gai Xun: "My military review is like this—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Colonel Who Punishes the Barbarians Gai Xun, "My military display is like this—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣聞先王□翟德不觀兵。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has heard that the ancient kings □ displayed virtue and did not observe troops.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have heard that the ancient kings who displayed their virtue did not review troops.

sentences.zh: 今寇在遠而設近陳，不足以昭果毅，只黷武耳！

translations.literal: Now the bandits are far away yet you set up a formation nearby—this is insufficient to display resolution and courage, and is only a debasement of arms!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are far away, yet you array troops nearby—this does not show resolve and courage; it only debases the use of arms!

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Well said!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well said!

sentences.zh: 恨見君晚，群臣初無是言也。

translations.literal: I regret meeting you so late—the ministers never said such things before.
translations.idiomatic: I only wish I had met you sooner—none of my ministers ever spoke to me this way before.

sentences.zh: 」勳謂袁紹曰：「上甚聰明，但蔽於左右耳。

translations.literal: " Xun said to Yuan Shao: "His Majesty is very intelligent, but he is blinded by those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: " Gai Xun told Yuan Shao, "The emperor is very intelligent, but he is blinded by those around him.

sentences.zh: 」與紹謀共誅嬖倖，蹇碩懼，出勳為京兆尹。

translations.literal: " He plotted with Shao to execute the favorites together; Jian Shuo was afraid and had Xun transferred out to be Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: " He and Yuan Shao plotted to kill the emperor's favorites together; Jian Shuo, alarmed, had Gai Xun transferred out to serve as intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王國圍陳倉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wang Guo besieged Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wang Guo besieged Chencang.

sentences.zh: 詔復拜皇甫嵩為左將軍，督前將軍董卓，合兵四萬人以拒之。

translations.literal: An edict reappointed Huangfu Song as General of the Left to supervise the Forward General Dong Zhuo, combining their forces to forty thousand men to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reappointed Huangfu Song as general of the left to command Forward General Dong Zhuo; together they fielded forty thousand men to oppose Wang Guo.

sentences.zh: 張純與丘力居鈔略青、徐、幽、冀四州；

translations.literal: Zhang Chun and Qiu Liju raided and plundered the four provinces of Qing, Xu, You, and Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun and Qiu Liju raided Qing, Xu, You, and Ji provinces;

sentences.zh: 詔騎都尉公孫瓚討之。

translations.literal: an edict ordered the Commandant of Cavalry Gongsun Zan to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict ordered Commandant of Cavalry Gongsun Zan to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 瓚與戰於屬國石門，純等大敗，棄妻子，逾塞走；

translations.literal: Zan fought them at Shimen in the Dependent State; Zhang Chun and the others were utterly defeated, abandoned their wives and children, and fled over the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan fought them at Shimen in the dependent state; Zhang Chun and his allies were routed, abandoned their families, and fled across the frontier;

sentences.zh: 悉得所略男女。

translations.literal: all the men and women they had carried off were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: recovering all the men and women they had seized.

sentences.zh: 瓚深入無繼，反為丘力居等所圍於遼西管子城，二百餘日，糧盡眾潰，士卒死者什五六。

translations.literal: Zan pressed deep in without support and was instead surrounded by Qiu Liju and the others at Guanzicheng in Liaoxi; after more than two hundred days his provisions were exhausted and his force collapsed, and five or six tenths of his soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan pressed deep into enemy territory without support and was surrounded by Qiu Liju and others at Guanzicheng in Liaoxi; after more than two hundred days his provisions ran out and his army collapsed, and five or six tenths of his soldiers perished.

sentences.zh: 董卓謂皇甫嵩曰：「陳倉危急，請速救之。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo said to Huangfu Song: "Chencang is in dire peril—please rescue it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo said to Huangfu Song, "Chencang is in grave danger—please rescue it at once.

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Song said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Huangfu Song said, "No.

sentences.zh: 百戰百勝，不如不戰而屈人兵。

translations.literal: A hundred battles and a hundred victories are inferior to subduing the enemy's troops without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred victories in a hundred battles are not as good as breaking the enemy's will to fight without fighting at all.

sentences.zh: 陳倉雖小，城守固備，未易可拔。

translations.literal: Though Chencang is small, its defenses are firm and well prepared—it is not easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: Chencang is small, but its defenses are strong and well prepared—it will not fall easily.

sentences.zh: 王國雖強，攻陳倉不下，其眾必疲，疲而擊之，全勝之道也，將何救焉！

translations.literal: Though Wang Guo is strong, if he cannot take Chencang his force will certainly grow weary; strike them when weary—that is the way to complete victory. What need is there to rescue!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo may be strong, but if he cannot take Chencang his men will wear themselves out; strike them when they are exhausted—that is the way to total victory. Why rush to the rescue!

sentences.zh: 」國攻陳倉八十餘日，不拔。

translations.literal: " Wang Guo besieged Chencang for more than eighty days without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Guo besieged Chencang for more than eighty days without success.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，國眾疲敝，解圍去，皇甫嵩進兵擊之。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Wang Guo's force was worn out; he lifted the siege and departed, and Huangfu Song advanced to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, Wang Guo's army was exhausted; he raised the siege and withdrew, and Huangfu Song advanced to attack.

sentences.zh: 董卓曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo said: "You must not.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo said, "You must not.

sentences.zh: 兵法，窮寇勿迫，歸眾勿追。

translations.literal: In the art of war: do not press a cornered foe; do not pursue troops returning home.
translations.idiomatic: The art of war says: do not press a cornered enemy, and do not pursue troops on their way home.

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Song said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Huangfu Song said, "No.

sentences.zh: 前吾不擊，避其銳也；

translations.literal: Before I did not strike because I was avoiding their keen edge;
translations.idiomatic: Before I held back to avoid their peak strength;

sentences.zh: 今而擊之，待其衰也；

translations.literal: now I strike because I am waiting for their decline;
translations.idiomatic: now I strike because I am waiting for their decline;

sentences.zh: 所擊疲師，非歸眾也；

translations.literal: what I strike is a weary force, not troops returning home;
translations.idiomatic: what I am attacking is an exhausted army, not men marching home;

sentences.zh: 國眾且走，莫有鬥志，以整擊亂，非窮寇也。

translations.literal: Wang Guo's force is about to flee and has no fighting spirit; to strike disorder with order is not pressing a cornered foe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo's men are already on the run and have no will to fight; striking disorder with an orderly force is not pressing a cornered enemy.

sentences.zh: 」遂獨進擊之，使卓為後拒，連戰，大破之，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: " He thereupon advanced alone to attack them, had Zhuo cover the rear, fought in succession, and routed them utterly, taking more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: " He then advanced alone to attack, had Dong Zhuo cover the rear, fought several engagements in succession, and routed the enemy completely, taking more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 卓大慚恨，由是與嵩有隙。

translations.literal: Zhuo was deeply ashamed and resentful; from this he bore a grudge against Song.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was deeply humiliated and resentful, and from this time bore a grudge against Huangfu Song.

sentences.zh: 韓遂等共廢王國，而劫故信都令漢陽閻忠使督統諸部。

translations.literal: Han Sui and the others jointly deposed Wang Guo and coerced Yan Zhong of Hanyang, former magistrate of Xindu, to command and oversee the various divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui and his allies jointly deposed Wang Guo and forced Yan Zhong of Hanyang, former magistrate of Xindu, to take command of the various divisions.

sentences.zh: 忠病死，遂等稍爭權利，更相殺害，由是寢衰。

translations.literal: Zhong died of illness; Sui and the others gradually quarreled over power and killed one another in turn, and from this their strength steadily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhong died of illness; Han Sui and the others then quarreled over power and killed one another, and from that point their movement steadily weakened.

sentences.zh: 幽州牧劉虞到部，遣使至鮮卑中，告以利害，責使送張舉、張純首，厚加購嘗。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu, Governor of You Province, reached his post, he sent envoys among the Xianbei, explained the advantages and disadvantages to them, demanded that they send the heads of Zhang Ju and Zhang Chun, and offered rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When You Province governor Liu Yu reached his post, he sent envoys among the Xianbei, explained the stakes to them, demanded the heads of Zhang Ju and Zhang Chun, and offered generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 丘力居等聞虞至，喜，各遣譯自歸。

translations.literal: When Qiu Liju and the others heard that Yu had arrived, they were pleased and each sent interpreters to submit of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Liju and the others heard that Liu Yu had arrived, they were pleased and each sent envoys to submit voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 舉、純走出塞，餘皆降散。

translations.literal: Ju and Chun fled beyond the frontier; the rest all surrendered and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju and Zhang Chun fled beyond the frontier; the rest surrendered and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 虞上罷諸屯兵，但留降虜校尉公孫瓚，將步騎萬人屯右北平。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized to disband the various garrison troops, retaining only the Colonel Who Subdues the Captives Gongsun Zan with ten thousand infantry and cavalry stationed at Right Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu memorialized to disband the various garrison forces, keeping only Colonel Who Subdues the Captives Gongsun Zan with ten thousand infantry and cavalry stationed at Right Beiping.

sentences.zh: 三月，張純客王政殺純，送首詣虞。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wang Zheng, a retainer of Zhang Chun, killed Chun and sent his head to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhang Chun's retainer Wang Zheng killed him and sent his head to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚志欲掃滅烏桓，而虞欲以恩信招降，由是與瓚有隙。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan was intent on exterminating the Wuhuan, whereas Yu wished to win them over through kindness and trustworthiness; from this he bore a rift with Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan was determined to exterminate the Wuhuan, while Liu Yu wished to win them over through kindness and trust; from this the two men fell out.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month, bingzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day, bingzi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太尉馬日磾免；

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Ma Midi was dismissed from office;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Ma Midi was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 遣使即拜幽州牧劉虞為太尉，封容丘侯。

translations.literal: an envoy was sent to appoint on the spot the Governor of You Province, Liu Yu, as Grand Commandant and enfeoff him as Marquis of Rongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: and an envoy was dispatched to appoint Liu Yu, Governor of You Province, Grand Commandant on the spot and enfeoff him as Marquis of Rongqiu.

sentences.zh: 蹇碩忌大將軍進，與諸常侍共說帝遣進西擊韓遂；

translations.literal: Jian Shuo resented the Grand General He Jin and, together with the various Regular Attendants, urged the emperor to send Jin west to attack Han Sui;
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shuo bore a grudge against Grand General He Jin and, together with the eunuch Regular Attendants, persuaded the emperor to send Jin west to campaign against Han Sui;

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: the emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 進陰知其謀，奏遣袁紹收徐、兗二州兵，須紹還而西，以稽行期。

translations.literal: Jin secretly knew their plot and memorialized that Yuan Shao be sent to gather the troops of Xu and Yan provinces, so that he would not march west until Shao returned, thereby delaying the departure date.
translations.idiomatic: Jin secretly learned of the plot and memorialized that Yuan Shao be sent to gather troops from Xu and Yan provinces, so that he would not march west until Shao returned—thus delaying the date of departure.

sentences.zh: 初，帝數失皇子，何皇后生子辯，養於道人史子眇家，號曰「史侯」。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had repeatedly lost imperial sons. Empress He bore a son, Bian, who was raised in the household of the Daoist Shi Zimiao and was called the "Marquis of Shi."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had lost several imperial sons in succession. Empress He gave birth to a son, Bian, who was raised in the household of the Daoist Shi Zimiao and was known as the "Marquis of Shi."

sentences.zh: 王美人生子協，董太后自養之，號曰「董侯」。

translations.literal: The Beautiful Lady Wang bore a son, Xie, whom Empress Dowager Dong herself raised; he was called the "Marquis of Dong."
translations.idiomatic: The Beautiful Lady Wang bore a son, Xie, whom Empress Dowager Dong raised herself; he was known as the "Marquis of Dong."

sentences.zh: 群臣請立太子。

translations.literal: The ministers requested that a crown prince be established.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials petitioned to name a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝以辯輕佻無威儀，欲立協，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Bian frivolous and lacking in dignified bearing and wished to establish Xie, but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded Bian as frivolous and lacking in dignified bearing and wished to make Xie heir, but he hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 會疾篤，屬協於蹇碩。

translations.literal: When his illness became grave, he entrusted Xie to Jian Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical, he entrusted Xie to Jian Shuo.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝崩於嘉德殿。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the emperor died in Jiade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day, the emperor died in Jiade Hall.

sentences.zh: 碩時在內，欲先誅何進而立協，使人迎進，欲與計事；

translations.literal: Shuo was then inside the palace and wished first to execute He Jin and establish Xie; he sent someone to summon Jin, intending to consult with him on affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was then inside the palace and wished first to kill He Jin and enthrone Xie; he sent someone to summon Jin, intending to discuss affairs with him;

sentences.zh: 進即駕往。

translations.literal: Jin immediately took his carriage and went.
translations.idiomatic: Jin at once set out in his carriage.

sentences.zh: 碩司馬潘隱與進早舊，迎而目之。

translations.literal: Shuo's Major Pan Yin had long been on familiar terms with Jin; he met him and signaled with his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's Major Pan Yin had been on friendly terms with Jin for years; he met him and signaled with his eyes.

sentences.zh: 進驚，馳從儳道歸營，引兵入屯百郡邸，因稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Jin was alarmed, galloped back to camp by a side passage, led troops to encamp at the Lodge of the Hundred Commanderies, and then pleaded illness and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Jin galloped back to camp by a side passage, led troops to encamp at the Lodge of the Hundred Commanderies, and then pleaded illness and refused to enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 戊午，皇子辯即皇帝位，年十四。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the imperial son Bian ascended the imperial throne; he was fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day, the imperial son Bian ascended the throne at the age of fourteen.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后臨朝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager presided over court.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager assumed regency over the court.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元為光熹。

translations.literal: There was an amnesty for all under Heaven, and the era name was changed to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 封皇弟協為渤海王。

translations.literal: The emperor's younger brother Xie was enfeoffed as King of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's younger brother Xie was enfeoffed as King of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 協年九歲。

translations.literal: Xie was nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was nine years old.

sentences.zh: 以後將軍袁隗為太傅，與大將軍何進參錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Rear General Yuan Wei was made Grand Tutor and, together with the Grand General He Jin, participated in recording the affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Yuan Wei was appointed Grand Tutor and, together with Grand General He Jin, was made to participate in the recording of Masters of Writing affairs.

sentences.zh: 進既秉朝政，忿蹇碩圖己，陰規誅之。

translations.literal: Once Jin held the reins of court government, he resented Jian Shuo's plot against him and secretly planned to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jin held power at court, he resented Jian Shuo's plot against him and secretly planned his execution.

sentences.zh: 袁紹因進親客張津，勸進悉誅諸宦官。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao, through Jin's intimate client Zhang Jin, urged Jin to execute all the palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Through Jin's intimate client Zhang Jin, Yuan Shao urged Jin to execute all the palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 進以袁氏累世貴寵，而紹與從弟虎賁中郎將術皆為豪桀所歸，信而用之。

translations.literal: Jin, because the Yuan clan had enjoyed honor and favor for generations and because both Shao and his cousin, the Colonel of the Rapid Tiger Guards Yuan Shu, were men to whom the bold and outstanding rallied, trusted and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Yuan clan had enjoyed honor and favor for generations, and because both Shao and his cousin Yuan Shu, Colonel of the Rapid Tiger Guards, were men whom the bold and outstanding rallied to, Jin trusted and employed them.

sentences.zh: 復博征智謀之士何顒、荀攸及河南鄭泰等二十餘人，以顒為北軍中候，攸為黃門侍郎，泰為尚書，與同腹心。

translations.literal: He further broadly recruited men of wisdom and counsel—He Yong, Xun You, Zheng Tai of Henan, and more than twenty others—appointing Yong Commandant of the Northern Army, You Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Tai Master of Writing, and treating them as his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited broadly such men of counsel as He Yong, Xun You, and Zheng Tai of Henan—more than twenty in all—appointing Yong Commandant of the Northern Army, You Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Tai Master of Writing, and treating them as his trusted inner circle.

sentences.zh: 攸，爽之從孫也。

translations.literal: You was a grandnephew of Xun Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: You was a grandnephew of Xun Shuang.

sentences.zh: 蹇碩疑不自安，與中常侍趙忠、宋典等書曰：「大將軍兄弟秉國專朝，今與天下黨人謀誅先帝左右，掃滅我曹，但以碩典禁兵，故且沉吟。

translations.literal: Jian Shuo, uneasy with suspicion, wrote to the Regular Attendants Zhao Zhong, Song Dian, and others, saying: "The Grand General and his brothers hold the state and monopolize the court. They are now plotting with partisans throughout the realm to execute those who stood close to the late emperor and to sweep us away—but because Shuo commands the forbidden troops, they are still hesitating.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy with suspicion, Jian Shuo wrote to the Regular Attendants Zhao Zhong, Song Dian, and others: "The Grand General and his brothers monopolize state power at court. They are now plotting with partisans throughout the realm to kill those who stood close to the late emperor and wipe us out—but because Shuo commands the forbidden troops, they are still hesitating.

sentences.zh: 今宜共閉上閣，急捕誅之。

translations.literal: Now we should together shut the upper gate and urgently seize and execute them."
translations.idiomatic: We should now together shut the upper gate and urgently seize and kill them."

sentences.zh: 」中常侍郭勝，進同郡人也，太后及進之貴幸，勝有力焉，故親信何氏；

translations.literal: The Regular Attendant Guo Sheng was a man of the same commandery as Jin; in the empress dowager's and Jin's rise to favor, Sheng had exerted himself greatly, and so he was intimate with the He clan;
translations.idiomatic: The Regular Attendant Guo Sheng was a fellow townsman of Jin; he had done much to advance the empress dowager and Jin to favor, and so he was close to the He clan;

sentences.zh: 與趙忠等議，不從碩計，而以其書示進。

translations.literal: he discussed the matter with Zhao Zhong and the others, did not follow Shuo's plan, and instead showed the letter to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: he consulted with Zhao Zhong and the others, rejected Shuo's plan, and showed the letter to Jin instead.

sentences.zh: 庚午，進使黃門令收碩，誅之，因悉領其屯兵。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Jin had the Bearer of the Yellow Gates seize Shuo and execute him, and thereby took over all his encamped troops.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day, Jin had the Bearer of the Yellow Gates seize Shuo and execute him, and thereby took command of all his encamped troops.

sentences.zh: 票騎將軍董重，與何進權勢相害，中官挾重以為黨助。

translations.literal: The General of Fast Cavalry Dong Chong was at odds with He Jin in power and influence, and the palace eunuchs relied on Chong as a partisan ally.
translations.idiomatic: General of Fast Cavalry Dong Chong was at odds with He Jin in power, and the palace eunuchs relied on Chong as their partisan ally.

sentences.zh: 董太后每欲參干政事，何太后輒相禁塞，董後忿恚詈曰：「汝今□舟張，怙汝兄耶！

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Dong often wished to interfere in government affairs, but Empress Dowager He always blocked her. Empress Dong, furious, cursed, saying: "You are arrogant now—do you rely on your brother!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Dong often wished to meddle in government affairs, but Empress Dowager He always blocked her. Empress Dong, furious, cursed her: "You are insufferably arrogant now—are you relying on your brother!

sentences.zh: 吾敕票騎斷何進頭，如反手耳！

translations.literal: If I order the General of Fast Cavalry to cut off He Jin's head, it will be like turning over my hand!"
translations.idiomatic: If I order the General of Fast Cavalry to cut off He Jin's head, it will be as easy as turning over my hand!"

sentences.zh: 」何太后聞之，以告進。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager He heard this, she told Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager He heard this, she told Jin.

sentences.zh: 五月，進與三公共奏：「孝仁皇后使故中常侍夏惲等交通州郡，辜較財利，悉入西省。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Jin and the Three Excellencies jointly memorialized: "The Xiaoren Empress had the former Regular Attendant Xia Yun and others deal with the provinces and commanderies, extort profit, and send it all into the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Jin and the Three Excellencies jointly memorialized: "Empress Xiaoren had the former Regular Attendant Xia Yun and others traffic with the provinces and commanderies, extort wealth, and funnel it all into the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 故事，蕃後不得留京師；

translations.literal: By precedent, empresses dowager of a different clan may not remain in the capital;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, empresses dowager of a different clan may not remain in the capital;

sentences.zh: 請遷宮本國。

translations.literal: we request that she be moved back to her native state."
translations.idiomatic: we request that she be moved back to her native fief."

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，進舉兵圍票騎府，收董重，免官，自殺。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Jin raised troops and besieged the mansion of the General of Fast Cavalry, seized Dong Chong, removed him from office, and Chong killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day, Jin raised troops and besieged the mansion of the General of Fast Cavalry, seized Dong Chong, stripped him of office, and Chong killed himself.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛亥，董後憂怖，暴崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinhai, Empress Dong, gripped by fear and dread, died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinhai day, Empress Dowager Dong, gripped by fear and dread, died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 民間由是不附何氏。

translations.literal: From this the common people ceased to attach themselves to the He clan.
translations.idiomatic: From this the common people ceased to rally to the He clan.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，葬孝靈皇帝於文陵。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Emperor Xiaoling was buried at Wenling.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, Emperor Ling was buried at Wenling.

sentences.zh: 何進懲蹇碩之謀，稱疾，不入陪喪，又不送山陵。

translations.literal: He Jin, mindful of Jian Shuo's plot, pleaded illness, did not enter to attend the mourning, and did not escort the tomb to the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Jian Shuo's plot, He Jin pleaded illness, did not attend the mourning rites, and did not escort the imperial tomb to the hills.

sentences.zh: 大水。

translations.literal: There were great floods.
translations.idiomatic: There were severe floods.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，徙渤海王協為陳留王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the King of Bohai, Xie, was moved to be King of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, King Xie of Bohai was demoted to King of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 司徒丁宮罷。

translations.literal: The Minister over the Masses Ding Gong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Ding Gong was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 袁紹復說何進曰：「前竇武欲誅內寵而反為所害者，但坐言語漏洩；

translations.literal: Yuan Shao again urged He Jin, saying: "Formerly Dou Wu wished to execute the inner favorites but was instead harmed by them—this was solely because word leaked out;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao again urged He Jin: "When Dou Wu wished to execute the inner favorites but was instead destroyed by them, it was solely because word leaked out;

sentences.zh: 五營兵士皆畏服中人，而竇氏反用之，自取禍滅。

translations.literal: the soldiers of the Five Camps all feared and submitted to the inner attendants, yet the Dou clan instead employed them and brought ruin on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: the soldiers of the Five Camps all feared and submitted to the inner attendants, yet the Dou clan employed them anyway and brought ruin on themselves.

sentences.zh: 今將軍兄弟並領勁兵，部曲將吏皆英俊名士，樂盡力命，事在掌握，此天贊之時也。

translations.literal: Now the general and his brothers together command crack troops; the officers and clerks of their staffs are all outstanding scholars and gentlemen who delight in giving their utmost; the matter is in your grasp—this is a time Heaven assists.
translations.idiomatic: Now you and your brothers command crack troops together; the officers on your staffs are all outstanding scholars and gentlemen eager to give their utmost; the matter is in your hands—this is a moment Heaven itself favors.

sentences.zh: 將軍宜一為天下除患，以垂名後世，不可失也！

translations.literal: The general ought at once to remove the scourge for all under Heaven and leave his name to posterity—you must not let this pass!"
translations.idiomatic: You ought at once to remove this scourge for the realm and leave your name to posterity—you must not let this chance slip by!"

sentences.zh: 」進乃白太后，請盡罷中常侍以下，以三署郎補其處。

translations.literal: Jin then reported to the empress dowager and requested that all Regular Attendants and below be entirely dismissed and that gentlemen of the Three Bureaus fill their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then reported to the empress dowager and asked that all Regular Attendants and below be dismissed and replaced with gentlemen of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 太后不聽，曰：「中官統領禁省，自古及今，漢家故事，不可廢也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager would not listen and said: "Palace eunuchs have commanded the forbidden quarters from antiquity to the present—it is Han house precedent and cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager refused and said: "Palace eunuchs have commanded the forbidden quarters from antiquity to the present—it is Han precedent and cannot be abolished.

sentences.zh: 且先帝新棄天下，我奈何楚楚與士人共對事乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, the late emperor has only just left the realm—how can I fussily face affairs together with scholar-officials!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the late emperor has only just departed—how can I sit here fussing over affairs with scholar-officials!"

sentences.zh: 」進難違太后意，且欲誅其放縱者。

translations.literal: Jin found it hard to go against the empress dowager's wish and wished only to execute those who were licentious and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Jin found it hard to defy the empress dowager and wished only to execute those who were licentious and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 紹以為中官親近至尊，出納號令，今不悉廢，後必為患。

translations.literal: Shao held that the palace eunuchs were intimate with the supreme ruler, issued and received orders and commands—if they were not all abolished now, they would surely become a scourge later.
translations.idiomatic: Shao argued that the palace eunuchs were intimate with the sovereign and controlled the issuing and receiving of orders—if they were not all abolished now, they would surely become a scourge later.

sentences.zh: 而太后母舞陽君及何苗數受諸宦官賂遣，知進欲誅之。

translations.literal: But the empress dowager's mother, the Lady of Wuyang, and He Miao had repeatedly received bribes and gifts from the various eunuchs and knew that Jin wished to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: But the empress dowager's mother, the Lady of Wuyang, and He Miao had repeatedly accepted bribes from the eunuchs and knew that Jin wished to kill them.

sentences.zh: 數白太后為其障蔽；

translations.literal: They repeatedly told the empress dowager to shield them;
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly urged the empress dowager to shield the eunuchs;

sentences.zh: 又言：「大將軍專殺左右，擅權以弱社稷。

translations.literal: they also said: "The Grand General kills those close to the throne on his own authority and monopolizes power to weaken the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: and they also said: "The Grand General kills those close to the throne on his own authority and monopolizes power to weaken the state."

sentences.zh: 」太后疑以為然。

translations.literal: The empress dowager suspected that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager came to suspect that this was true.

sentences.zh: 進新貴，素敬憚中官，雖外慕大名而內不能斷，故事久不決。

translations.literal: Jin had only recently risen to honor and had always respected and feared the palace eunuchs; though outwardly he coveted a great reputation, inwardly he could not decide, and for a long time the matter went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had only recently risen to power and had always respected and feared the palace eunuchs; though he coveted a great reputation outwardly, inwardly he could not make up his mind, and for a long time the affair remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 紹等又為畫策，多召四方猛將及諸豪傑，使並引兵向京城，以脅太后；

translations.literal: Shao and the others again devised a plan: to summon many fierce generals from the four quarters and various bold heroes, have them all lead troops toward the capital, and thereby coerce the empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: Shao and the others devised another plan: summon many fierce generals from the four quarters and various bold heroes, have them all march on the capital with troops, and thereby coerce the empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 進然之；

translations.literal: Jin approved this;
translations.idiomatic: Jin agreed;

sentences.zh: 主簿廣陵陳琳諫曰：「諺稱『掩目捕雀』，夫微物尚不可欺以得志，況國之大事，其要以詐立乎！

translations.literal: the Registrar Chen Lin of Guangling remonstrated, saying: "A proverb says, 'Cover your eyes to catch sparrows'—even the smallest creatures cannot be deceived with impunity and still succeed, how much less a great affair of state—can its foundation be laid by deceit!
translations.idiomatic: but Registrar Chen Lin of Guangling remonstrated: "A proverb says, 'Cover your eyes to catch sparrows'—even the smallest creatures cannot be tricked with impunity, how much less a great affair of state! Can its foundation be laid by deceit?"

sentences.zh: 今將軍總皇威，握兵要，龍驤虎步，高下在心，此猶鼓洪爐燎毛髮耳。

translations.literal: Now the general commands imperial majesty and holds the keys to the army—dragon soaring, tiger striding; what is high or low lies in your heart—this is like stirring a great furnace to singe hair.
translations.idiomatic: You now command imperial authority and hold the keys to military power—like a dragon soaring or a tiger striding, what rises or falls lies in your heart alone. This would be as easy as stirring a great furnace to singe hair.

sentences.zh: 但當速發雷霆，行權立斷，則天人順之。

translations.literal: You need only swiftly unleash thunder, exercise power, and decide at once—then Heaven and men will follow.
translations.idiomatic: You need only swiftly unleash thunder, exercise decisive authority, and act at once—then Heaven and men alike will follow.

sentences.zh: 而反委釋利器，更征外助，大兵聚會，強者為雄，所謂倒持干戈，授人以柄，功必不成，只為亂階耳！

translations.literal: Yet instead you cast aside sharp weapons and seek aid from outside; when great armies gather, the strong become hegemon—this is what is called holding the spear reversed and handing the handle to another. Success is sure not to come; you will only create the steps to chaos!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet instead you cast aside your weapons and seek outside help. When great armies gather, the strong become hegemons—this is what is called holding the spear by the blade and handing the handle to another. You are sure to fail and will only create the prelude to chaos!"

sentences.zh: 」進不聽。

translations.literal: Jin would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin would not listen.

sentences.zh: 典軍校尉曹操聞而笑曰：「宦者之官，古今宜有，但世主不當假之權寵，使至於此。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Imperial Insignia Cao Cao heard this and laughed, saying: "The office of palace eunuchs has been appropriate in every age, but a ruler of the age ought not to lend them power and favor until matters reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Imperial Insignia Cao Cao heard this and laughed: "The office of palace eunuch has existed in every age, but rulers ought not to lend them power and favor until matters reach this pass.

sentences.zh: 既治其罪，當誅元惡，一獄吏足矣，何至紛紛召外兵乎！

translations.literal: Once their crime is judged, the chief culprit ought to be executed—a single prison clerk would suffice. Why must you in confusion summon outside troops!
translations.idiomatic: Once their crime is established, the chief culprits should be executed—a single prison clerk would suffice. Why must you in confusion summon outside troops!

sentences.zh: 欲盡誅之，事必宣露，吾見其敗也。

translations.literal: If you wish to execute them all, the affair is sure to leak out—I see that you will fail."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to kill them all, the affair is sure to leak out—I see that you will fail."

sentences.zh: 初，靈帝征董卓為少府，卓上書言：「所將湟中義從及秦、胡兵皆詣臣言：『牢直不畢，稟賜斷絕，妻子饑凍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Ling had summoned Dong Zhuo to be Minister Steward. Zhuo memorialized, saying: "The voluntary followers from Huangzhong and the Qin and Hu troops I command have all come to me saying: 'Our salary rations are not paid in full, stipends and gifts have been cut off, and our wives and children hunger and freeze.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Ling had summoned Dong Zhuo to serve as Minister Steward. Zhuo memorialized: "The voluntary followers from Huangzhong and the Qin and Hu troops under my command have all come to me saying: 'Our salary rations are not paid in full, stipends and gifts have been cut off, and our wives and children hunger and freeze.

sentences.zh: 』率挽臣車，使不得行。

translations.literal: ' They have seized and held back my carriage so that I cannot proceed.
translations.idiomatic: ' They have seized my carriage and would not let me proceed.

sentences.zh: 羌、胡憋腸狗態，臣不能禁止，輒將順安慰。

translations.literal: The Qiang and Hu are ill-tempered and dog-like in conduct; I cannot restrain them and have only gone along to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and Hu are savage and dog-like in temper; I cannot restrain them and have only gone along to placate them.

sentences.zh: 增異復上。

translations.literal: I have filed another memorial asking for an increase."
translations.idiomatic: I have filed another memorial asking for additional funds."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不能制。

translations.literal: The court could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: The court could not control him.

sentences.zh: 及帝寢疾，璽書拜卓并州牧，今以兵屬皇甫嵩。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell gravely ill, an imperial-seal letter appointed Zhuo Governor of Bing Province and ordered that his troops be placed under Huangfu Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, an imperial-seal letter appointed Zhuo Governor of Bing Province and ordered that his troops be transferred to Huangfu Song.

sentences.zh: 卓復上書言：「臣誤蒙天恩，掌戎十年，士卒大小，相狎彌久，戀臣畜養之恩，為臣奮一旦之命，乞將之北州，效力邊垂。

translations.literal: Zhuo again memorialized, saying: "Your servant has undeservedly received Heaven's grace and commanded troops for ten years. Officers and men, great and small, have grown familiar over long years; they cherish the kindness of my nurturing and would stake their lives for me in a single day. I beg to lead them to the northern province and serve at the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo memorialized again: "Your servant has undeservedly received Heaven's grace and commanded troops for ten years. Officers and men, great and small, have grown familiar over the years; they cherish the kindness of my care and would stake their lives for me in a single day. I beg to lead them to the northern province and serve on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」嵩從子酈說嵩曰：「天下兵柄，在大人與董卓耳。

translations.literal: Song's nephew's son Li urged Song, saying: "The military authority of all under Heaven lies with you, sir, and Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Song's grandnephew Li urged him: "The military authority of the realm lies with you and Dong Zhuo alone.

sentences.zh: 今怨隙已結，勢不俱存，卓被詔委兵而上書自請，此逆命也。

translations.literal: Now enmity has been formed and the two cannot both remain. Zhuo received the edict to surrender his troops yet memorialized asking on his own behalf—this is defiance of orders.
translations.idiomatic: Enmity has now been formed between you, and the two of you cannot both remain. Zhuo received the edict to surrender his troops yet memorialized asking to keep them—this is defiance of orders.

sentences.zh: 彼率京師政亂，故敢躊躇不進，此懷奸也。

translations.literal: He leads troops while the capital is in political turmoil, and so dares to hesitate and not advance—this is harboring treachery.
translations.idiomatic: He leads troops while the capital is in turmoil, and so dares to linger and not advance—this is harboring treachery.

sentences.zh: 二者，刑所不赦。

translations.literal: Both offenses are such as punishment does not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Both offenses are unpardonable under the law.

sentences.zh: 且其凶戾無親，將士不附。

translations.literal: Moreover, he is fierce and cruel and without kinship ties; officers and soldiers do not attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he is fierce, cruel, and without loyal ties; his officers and soldiers do not truly follow him.

sentences.zh: 大人今為元帥，杖國威以討之，上顯忠義，下除凶害，無不濟也。

translations.literal: You, sir, are now supreme commander; wielding the state's majesty to punish him, you will display loyalty and righteousness above and remove a vicious scourge below—nothing will fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: You are now supreme commander; wield the state's authority to punish him, display loyalty and righteousness above and remove a vicious scourge below—and nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「違命雖罪，專誅亦有責也。

translations.literal: Song said: "Defying orders is indeed a crime, but unauthorized execution also incurs blame.
translations.idiomatic: Song said: "Defying orders is indeed a crime, but unauthorized execution also brings blame.

sentences.zh: 不如顯奏其事，使朝廷裁之。

translations.literal: It would be better openly to memorialize the matter and let the court decide.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to memorialize the matter openly and let the court decide.

sentences.zh: 」乃上書以聞。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to report it.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to report it.

sentences.zh: 帝以讓卓。

translations.literal: The emperor reproved Zhuo on this account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproved Zhuo on this account.

sentences.zh: 卓亦不奉詔，駐兵河東以觀時變。

translations.literal: Zhuo also did not obey the edict and encamped his troops at Hedong to watch how the times changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo also refused to obey the edict and encamped his troops at Hedong to watch how events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 何進召卓使將兵詣京師。

translations.literal: He Jin summoned Zhuo to lead troops to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin summoned Zhuo to lead troops to the capital.

sentences.zh: 侍御史鄭泰諫曰：「董卓強忍寡義，志欲無厭，若借之朝政，授以大事，將恣凶欲，必危朝廷。

translations.literal: The Attendant Censor Zheng Tai remonstrated, saying: "Dong Zhuo is forcibly enduring and lacking in righteousness; his ambition is insatiable. If you lend him court government and entrust him with great affairs, he will indulge his vicious desires and is sure to endanger the court.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Zheng Tai remonstrated: "Dong Zhuo is brutal and faithless, his ambition insatiable. If you lend him a role in court government and entrust him with great affairs, he will indulge his vicious desires and is sure to endanger the court.

sentences.zh: 明公以親德之重，據阿衡之權，秉意獨斷，誅除有罪，誠不宜假卓以為資援也！

translations.literal: Your Excellency, by the weight of your kinship and virtue, holds the authority of Yi Yin; you ought to hold your will and decide alone, execute the guilty—truly you should not lend Zhuo as a resource and support!
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency, by the weight of your kinship and virtue, hold the authority of a chief minister; you ought to decide alone and execute the guilty—you truly should not use Zhuo as a resource!

sentences.zh: 且事留變生，殷鑒不遠，宜在速決。

translations.literal: Moreover, if affairs linger, change will arise—the mirror of recent warning is not far off; you ought to decide swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if affairs linger, change will arise—the lesson of recent history is not far off; you ought to decide swiftly.

sentences.zh: 」尚書盧植亦言不宜召卓，進皆不從。

translations.literal: The Master of Writing Lu Zhi also said that Zhuo ought not to be summoned; Jin would not listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Lu Zhi also said that Zhuo ought not to be summoned; Jin would not listen to any of them.

sentences.zh: 泰乃棄官去，謂荀攸曰：「何公未易輔也。

translations.literal: Tai then abandoned his office and left, saying to Xun You: "Lord He is not easy to assist."
translations.idiomatic: Tai then resigned his office and left, saying to Xun You: "Lord He is not easy to assist."

sentences.zh: 」進府掾王匡，騎都尉鮑信，皆泰山人，進使還鄉里募兵；

translations.literal: Jin's staff officer Wang Kuang and the Commandant of Cavalry Bao Xin were both men of Taishan; Jin sent them back to their home districts to raise troops;
translations.idiomatic: Jin's staff officer Wang Kuang and Commandant of Cavalry Bao Xin were both natives of Taishan; Jin sent them back to their home districts to raise troops;

sentences.zh: 並召工郡太守橋瑁屯成皋，使武猛都尉丁原將數千人寇河內，燒孟津，火照城中，皆以誅宦官為言。

translations.literal: and at the same time summoned the Administrator of Gong Commandery Qiao Mao to encamp at Chenggao, and had the Colonel of Martial Valor Ding Yuan lead several thousand men to raid Henei, burn Mengjin—the fire lighting up the city—and all spoke of executing the palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: and at the same time summoned Administrator Qiao Mao of Henei to encamp at Chenggao, and had Colonel of Martial Valor Ding Yuan lead several thousand men to raid Henei, burn Mengjin—the flames lighting up the city—and all proclaimed that their aim was to execute the palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 董卓聞召，即時就道，並上書曰：「中常侍張讓等，竊幸承寵，濁亂海內。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo heard the summons, he set out on the road at once and also memorialized, saying: "The Regular Attendants Zhang Rang and others have stolen favor and received indulgence, befouling and disordering all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo heard the summons, he set out at once and also memorialized: "The Regular Attendants Zhang Rang and others have stolen imperial favor and thrown the realm into chaos.

sentences.zh: 臣聞揚湯止沸，莫若支薪；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that to ladle boiling water to stop it from boiling is not as good as removing the firewood;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that ladling boiling water to stop it from boiling is not as good as removing the firewood;

sentences.zh: 潰癰雖痛，勝於內食。

translations.literal: lancing an abscess, though painful, is better than letting it fester inward.
translations.idiomatic: lancing an abscess, though painful, is better than letting it fester inward.

sentences.zh: 昔趙鞅興晉陽之甲以逐君側之惡，今臣輒鳴鐘鼓如雒陽，請收讓等以清奸穢！

translations.literal: Formerly Zhao Yang raised the troops of Jinyang to drive out evil at the ruler's side; now your servant will sound bells and drums toward Luoyang and request that Rang and the others be seized to purge treachery and filth!"
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhao Yang raised the troops of Jinyang to drive out evil at the ruler's side; now I shall sound bells and drums toward Luoyang and request that Rang and the others be seized to purge treachery and filth!"

sentences.zh: 」太后猶不從。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager still refused.

sentences.zh: 何苗謂進曰：「始共從南陽來，俱以貪賤依省內以致富貴，國家之事，亦何容易。

translations.literal: He Miao said to Jin: "At first we came together from Nanyang, both relying on the inner quarters from a state of greed and low status to attain wealth and honor—affairs of state are not so easily managed.
translations.idiomatic: He Miao said to Jin: "At first we came together from Nanyang, both of us rising from poverty by relying on the inner quarters to attain wealth and honor—affairs of state are not so easily managed.

sentences.zh: 覆水不收，宜深思之，且與省內和也。

translations.literal: Spilled water cannot be gathered back—you ought to think deeply on this and make peace with the inner quarters."
translations.idiomatic: Spilled water cannot be gathered back—you ought to think deeply on this and make peace with the inner quarters."

sentences.zh: 」卓至澠池，而進更狐疑，使諫議大夫種邵宣詔止之。

translations.literal: When Zhuo reached Mianchi, Jin grew still more hesitant and sent the Adviser Zhong Shao to proclaim an edict halting him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo reached Mianchi, Jin grew still more hesitant and sent Adviser Zhong Shao to proclaim an edict ordering him to halt.

sentences.zh: 卓不受詔，遂前至河南；

translations.literal: Zhuo did not accept the edict and advanced to Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo refused the edict and advanced to Henan;

sentences.zh: 邵迎勞之，因譬令還軍。

translations.literal: Shao went out to meet and welcome him and, by analogy and persuasion, ordered him to return his army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao went out to meet and welcome him and urged him by analogy to turn his army back.

sentences.zh: 卓疑有變，使其軍士以兵脅邵。

translations.literal: Zhuo suspected a trap and had his soldiers threaten Shao with weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo suspected a trap and had his soldiers threaten Shao with weapons.

sentences.zh: 邵怒，稱詔叱之，軍士皆披，遂前質責卓；

translations.literal: Shao was enraged, invoked the edict to rebuke them, and the soldiers all scattered; he then advanced and confronted Zhuo to his face;
translations.idiomatic: Shao was enraged, invoked the edict to rebuke them, and the soldiers all scattered; he then advanced and confronted Zhuo to his face;

sentences.zh: 卓辭屈，乃還軍夕陽亭。

translations.literal: Zhuo's words were defeated, and he returned his army to Xiyang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was put to silence and withdrew his army to Xiyang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 劭，暠之孫也。

translations.literal: Shao was a grandson of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was a grandson of Hao.

sentences.zh: 袁紹懼進變計，因脅之曰：「交構已成，形勢已露，將軍復欲何待而不早決之乎？

translations.literal: Yuan Shao feared that Jin would change his plan and therefore coerced him, saying: "The plot is already joined, the situation already exposed—what more does the general wish to wait for before deciding early?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao feared that Jin would change his mind and pressed him: "The plot is already in place and the situation exposed—what more are you waiting for before you decide?

sentences.zh: 事久變生，復為竇氏矣！

translations.literal: If affairs linger, change will arise—you will become another Dou clan!"
translations.idiomatic: If you delay, things will shift—you will become another Dou clan!"

sentences.zh: 」進於是以紹為司隸校尉，假節，專命擊斷；

translations.literal: Jin thereupon made Shao Director of the Retainers, with credential staff and sole authority to strike and judge;
translations.idiomatic: Jin thereupon appointed Shao Director of the Retainers, with credential staff and sole authority to strike and judge;

sentences.zh: 從事中郎王允為河南尹。

translations.literal: the Attendant Gentleman Wang Yun was made Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: and Attendant Gentleman Wang Yun was made Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 紹使雒陽方略武吏司察宦者，而促董卓等使馳驛上奏，欲進兵平樂觀。

translations.literal: Shao had strategic military clerks of Luoyang investigate the eunuchs and urged Dong Zhuo and the others to dispatch post-horses with memorials, intending to advance troops to the Pingle Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had strategic military clerks of Luoyang investigate the eunuchs and urged Dong Zhuo and the others to send urgent memorials by post relay, intending to advance troops to the Pingle Observatory.

sentences.zh: 太后乃恐，悉罷中常侍、小黃門使還裡捨，唯留進素所私人以守省中。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then grew afraid and dismissed all Regular Attendants and Junior Yellow Gates to return to their home quarters, keeping only Jin's longtime personal associates to guard the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager then grew afraid and dismissed all Regular Attendants and Junior Yellow Gates to their home quarters, keeping only Jin's longtime personal associates to guard the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 諸常侍、小黃門皆詣進謝罪，唯所措置。

translations.literal: All the Regular Attendants and Junior Yellow Gates came to Jin to beg forgiveness and left everything to his arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: All the Regular Attendants and Junior Yellow Gates came to Jin to beg forgiveness and left everything to his discretion.

sentences.zh: 進謂曰：「天下匈匈，正患諸君耳。

translations.literal: Jin said to them: "All under Heaven is in turmoil—the very scourge is you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said to them: "The realm is in turmoil, and you gentlemen are the very scourge.

sentences.zh: 今董卓垂至，諸君何不早各就國！

translations.literal: Now Dong Zhuo is about to arrive—why do you not each return early to your states!"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo is about to arrive—why do you not each return early to your fiefs!"

sentences.zh: 」袁紹勸進便於此決之，至於再三；

translations.literal: Yuan Shao urged Jin to decide the matter right then and there, even to the point of repeating it again and again;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao urged Jin to decide the matter then and there, repeating himself again and again;

sentences.zh: 進不許。

translations.literal: Jin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jin refused.

sentences.zh: 紹又為書告諸州郡，詐宣進意，使捕案中官親屬。

translations.literal: Shao also wrote to the various provinces and commanderies, falsely proclaiming Jin's intent and ordering the arrest and investigation of eunuch kin.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also wrote to the various provinces and commanderies, falsely proclaiming Jin's intent and ordering the arrest and investigation of eunuchs' kin.

sentences.zh: 進謀積日，頗洩，中官懼而思變。

translations.literal: Jin's plot accumulated over many days and leaked considerably; the palace eunuchs grew afraid and thought of changing course.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's plot had been brewing for days and leaked considerably; the palace eunuchs grew afraid and plotted a counterstroke.

sentences.zh: 張讓子婦，太后之妹也，讓向子婦叩頭曰：「老臣得罪，當與新婦俱歸私門。

translations.literal: Zhang Rang's daughter-in-law was the empress dowager's younger sister. Rang kowtowed to his daughter-in-law and said: "This old minister has offended and ought to return to private life together with my new daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang's daughter-in-law was the empress dowager's younger sister. Rang kowtowed to her and said: "This old minister has offended and ought to return to private life with my new daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 唯受恩累世，今當遠離宮殿，情懷戀戀，願復一入直，得暫奉望太后陛下顏色，然後退就溝壑，死不恨矣！

translations.literal: Only, having received favor for generations, I am now to leave the palace far behind; my feelings cling and linger. I wish to enter duty once more and be able briefly to behold the countenance of Her Majesty the Empress Dowager, and then withdraw to the ditches and gullies—I would die without regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Only, having received favor for generations, I must now leave the palace far behind, yet my heart clings to it. I beg to enter duty once more, if only briefly to behold the empress dowager's face, and then withdraw to my grave—I would die without regret!"

sentences.zh: 」子婦言於舞陽君，入白太后，乃詔諸常侍皆復入直。

translations.literal: The daughter-in-law spoke to the Lady of Wuyang, who entered and reported to the empress dowager; an edict was then issued that all Regular Attendants should return to duty.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter-in-law spoke to the Lady of Wuyang, who reported to the empress dowager; an edict was then issued ordering all Regular Attendants back to duty.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊辰，進入長樂宮，白太后，請盡誅諸常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuchen, Jin entered Changle Palace, reported to the empress dowager, and requested that all Regular Attendants be executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuchen day, Jin entered Changle Palace, reported to the empress dowager, and asked that all Regular Attendants be executed.

sentences.zh: 中常侍張讓、段珪相謂曰：「大將軍稱疾，不臨喪，不送葬，今欻入省，此意何為？

translations.literal: The Regular Attendants Zhang Rang and Duan Gui said to each other: "The Grand General pleaded illness, did not attend the mourning, and did not escort the burial—now he has suddenly entered the inner quarters. What is his intent?
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendants Zhang Rang and Duan Gui said to each other: "The Grand General pleaded illness, did not attend the mourning, and did not escort the burial—now he has suddenly entered the inner quarters. What does he intend?

sentences.zh: 竇氏事竟復起邪？

translations.literal: Is the affair of the Dou clan rising again?"
translations.idiomatic: Is the affair of the Dou clan rising again?"

sentences.zh: 」使潛聽，具聞其語。

translations.literal: They sent someone to listen secretly and heard the whole of their words.
translations.idiomatic: They sent someone to eavesdrop and heard everything.

sentences.zh: 乃率其黨數十人持兵竊自側闥入，伏省戶下，進出，因詐以太后詔召進，入坐省閣。

translations.literal: They then led several dozen of their partisans, weapons in hand, to steal in through the side gate, lay in ambush beneath the inner door, and when Jin came out, falsely summoned him with an empress dowager edict; he entered and sat in the inner gate-house.
translations.idiomatic: They then led several dozen armed partisans to steal in through the side gate and lay in ambush beneath the inner door; when Jin came out, they falsely summoned him with an empress dowager edict, and he entered and sat in the inner gate-house.

sentences.zh: 讓等詰進曰：「天下憒憒，亦非獨我曹罪也。

translations.literal: Rang and the others interrogated Jin, saying: "All under Heaven is in turmoil—this is not solely our crime.
translations.idiomatic: Rang and the others confronted Jin: "The realm is in turmoil—this is not solely our fault.

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗與太后不快，幾至成敗，我曹涕泣救解，各出家財千萬為禮，和悅上意，但欲托卿門戶耳。

translations.literal: The late emperor once had discord with the empress dowager, and matters nearly came to ruin; we wept and rescued the situation, each contributing tens of millions from family wealth as gifts to soothe the sovereign's mind—we only wished to entrust ourselves to your house.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor once quarreled with the empress dowager, and matters nearly came to ruin; we wept and rescued the situation, each contributing tens of millions from family wealth as gifts to soothe the sovereign's mind—we only wished to entrust ourselves to your house.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲滅我曹種族，不亦太甚乎！

translations.literal: Now you wish to exterminate our clans—is this not too extreme!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you wish to exterminate our clans—is this not too extreme!"

sentences.zh: 」於是尚方監渠穆拔劍斬進於嘉德殿前。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Director of the Imperial Workshop Qu Mu drew his sword and cut Jin down before Jiade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Director of the Imperial Workshop Qu Mu drew his sword and cut Jin down before Jiade Hall.

sentences.zh: 讓、珪等為詔，以故太尉樊陵為司隸校尉，少府許相為河南尹。
