translations.literal: Rang, Gui, and the others forged an edict appointing the former Grand Commandant Fan Ling as Director of the Retainers and the Minister Steward Xu Xiang as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Rang, Gui, and the others forged an edict appointing former Grand Commandant Fan Ling Director of the Retainers and Minister Steward Xu Xiang Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尚書得詔板，疑之，曰：「請大將軍出共議。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing received the edict board, suspected it, and said: "We request that the Grand General come out to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing received the edict board, grew suspicious, and said: "We request that the Grand General come out to deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 」中黃門以進頭擲與尚書曰：「何進謀反，已伏誅矣！

translations.literal: A Bearer of the Yellow Gates threw Jin's head to the Masters of Writing and said: "He Jin plotted rebellion and has already been executed!"
translations.idiomatic: A Bearer of the Yellow Gates threw Jin's head to the Masters of Writing and said: "He Jin plotted rebellion and has already been executed!"

sentences.zh: 進部曲將吳匡、張璋在外，聞進被害，欲引兵入宮，宮門閉。

translations.literal: Jin's staff generals Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang were outside; hearing that Jin had been killed, they wished to lead troops into the palace, but the palace gates were shut.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's staff generals Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang were outside; hearing that Jin had been killed, they tried to lead troops into the palace, but the palace gates were shut.

sentences.zh: 虎賁中郎將袁術與匡共斫攻之，中黃門持兵守閣。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Rapid Tiger Guards Yuan Shu joined Kuang in hacking and attacking; Bearers of the Yellow Gates held weapons and guarded the gate-house.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Rapid Tiger Guards Yuan Shu joined Kuang in hacking at the gates; Bearers of the Yellow Gates held weapons and guarded the gate-house.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，術因燒南宮青瑣門，欲以脅出讓等。

translations.literal: As dusk fell, Shu set fire to the Green Ring Gate of the Southern Palace, intending to coerce Rang and the others to come out.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk fell, Shu set fire to the Green Ring Gate of the Southern Palace, intending to force Rang and the others out.

sentences.zh: 讓等入白太后，言大將軍兵反，燒宮，攻尚書闥，因將太后、少帝及陳留王，劫省內官屬，從復道走北宮。

translations.literal: Rang and the others entered to report to the empress dowager that the Grand General's troops had rebelled, burned the palace, and attacked the Masters of Writing gate; they then took the empress dowager, the young emperor, and the King of Chenliu, seized the inner officials, and fled along the covered passage to the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rang and the others reported to the empress dowager that the Grand General's troops had rebelled, burned the palace, and attacked the Masters of Writing gate; they then seized the empress dowager, the young emperor, and the King of Chenliu, took the inner officials hostage, and fled along the covered passage to the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧植執戈於閣道窗下，仰數段珪；

translations.literal: The Master of Writing Lu Zhi held a halberd beneath the window of the covered passage and looked up to rebuke Duan Gui;
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Lu Zhi held a halberd beneath the window of the covered passage and looked up to rebuke Duan Gui;

sentences.zh: 珪懼，乃釋太后，太后投閣，得免。

translations.literal: Gui was afraid and released the empress dowager; the empress dowager threw herself into the gate-house and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was afraid and released the empress dowager; she threw herself into the gate-house and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 袁紹與叔父隗矯詔召樊陵、許相，斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao and his uncle Wei forged an edict summoning Fan Ling and Xu Xiang and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and his uncle Wei forged an edict summoning Fan Ling and Xu Xiang and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 紹及何苗引兵屯朱雀闕下，捕得趙忠等，斬之。

translations.literal: Shao and He Miao led troops to encamp below the Vermilion Bird Gate, captured Zhao Zhong and the others, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and He Miao led troops to encamp below the Vermilion Bird Gate, captured Zhao Zhong and the others, and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 吳匡等素怨苗不與進同心，而又疑其與宦官通謀，乃令軍中曰：「殺大將軍者，即車騎也，吏士能為報仇乎？

translations.literal: Wu Kuang and the others had long resented Miao for not sharing Jin's purpose and also suspected him of conspiring with the eunuchs; they therefore told the army: "The one who killed the Grand General is the General of Chariots and Cavalry—officers and soldiers, can you avenge him?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kuang and the others had long resented Miao for not sharing Jin's purpose and suspected him of conspiring with the eunuchs; they told the army: "The one who killed the Grand General is the General of Chariots and Cavalry—officers and soldiers, will you avenge him?"

sentences.zh: 」皆流涕曰：「願致死！

translations.literal: All wept and said: "We wish to die in the attempt!"
translations.idiomatic: All wept and said: "We will die in the attempt!"

sentences.zh: 」匡遂引兵與董卓弟奉車都尉旻攻殺苗，棄其屍於苑中。

translations.literal: Kuang then led troops with Dong Zhuo's younger brother, the Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Min, to attack and kill Miao and cast his corpse in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang then led troops with Dong Zhuo's younger brother Min, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, to attack and kill Miao and cast his corpse in the park.

sentences.zh: 紹遂閉北宮門，勒兵捕諸宦者，無少長皆殺之，凡二千餘人，或有無須而誤死者。

translations.literal: Shao then shut the Northern Palace gate, compelled his troops to seize all the eunuchs, and killed them without regard to age—more than two thousand in all; some who had no beard were mistakenly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then shut the Northern Palace gate and ordered his troops to seize all eunuchs and kill them without regard to age—more than two thousand in all; some beardless men were mistakenly killed as well.

sentences.zh: 紹因進兵排宮，或上端門屋，以攻省內。

translations.literal: Shao then advanced troops to force the palace; some climbed the roof of the Upper Gate to attack the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then advanced troops to force the palace; some climbed onto the Upper Gate roof to attack the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 庚午，張讓、段珪等困迫，遂將帝與陳留王數十人步出谷門，夜，至小平津，六璽不自隨，公卿無得從者，唯尚書盧植、河南中部掾閔貢夜至河上。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Zhang Rang, Duan Gui, and the others, hard pressed, then led the emperor and the King of Chenliu and several dozen others on foot out through Gumen; by night they reached Xiaoping Ford. The six seals did not accompany them of themselves; no excellencies or ministers could follow—only the Master of Writing Lu Zhi and the Central Adjutant of Henan Min Gong reached the river by night.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day, Zhang Rang, Duan Gui, and the others, hard pressed, led the emperor and the King of Chenliu and several dozen others on foot out through Gumen; by night they reached Xiaoping Ford. The six seals did not accompany them; no excellencies or ministers could follow—only Master of Writing Lu Zhi and Central Adjutant of Henan Min Gong reached the river by night.

sentences.zh: 貢厲聲質責讓等，且曰：「今不速死，吾將殺汝！

translations.literal: Gong rebuked Rang and the others in a harsh voice and said: "If you do not die swiftly now, I will kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: Gong rebuked Rang and the others in a harsh voice: "If you do not die swiftly now, I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 」因手劍斬數人。

translations.literal: He then personally drew his sword and cut down several men.
translations.idiomatic: He then personally drew his sword and cut down several men.

sentences.zh: 讓等惶怖，叉手再拜，叩頭向帝辭曰：「臣等死，陛下自愛！

translations.literal: Rang and the others were terrified; they clasped their hands, bowed twice, kowtowed toward the emperor, and took leave, saying: "We die—Your Majesty, take care of yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Rang and the others were terrified; they clasped their hands, bowed twice, kowtowed to the emperor, and took leave: "We die—Your Majesty, take care of yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」遂投河而死。

translations.literal: They then threw themselves into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: They then threw themselves into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 貢扶帝與陳留王夜步逐螢光南行，欲還宮，行數里，得民家露車，共乘之，至雒捨止，辛未，帝獨乘一馬，陳留王與貢共乘一馬，從雒捨南行，公卿稍有至者。

translations.literal: Gong supported the emperor and the King of Chenliu as they walked south by night following firefly light, wishing to return to the palace; after several li they obtained a commoner's open cart and rode it together to Luoshe and stopped. On the day xinwei, the emperor rode one horse alone; the King of Chenliu and Gong rode one horse together and went south from Luoshe; excellencies and ministers gradually began to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Gong supported the emperor and the King of Chenliu as they walked south by night following firefly light, wishing to return to the palace; after several li they found a commoner's open cart and rode it together to Luoshe and stopped. On xinwei day, the emperor rode one horse alone; the King of Chenliu and Gong shared one horse and went south from Luoshe; excellencies and ministers gradually began to arrive.

sentences.zh: 董卓至顯陽苑，遠見火起，知有變，引兵急進；

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo reached the Xianyang Park, saw fires rising in the distance, knew there was turmoil, and led his troops forward in haste;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo reached the Xianyang Park, saw fires rising in the distance, knew turmoil had broken out, and led his troops forward in haste;

sentences.zh: 未明，到城西，聞帝在北，因與公卿往奉迎於北芒阪下。

translations.literal: before dawn he reached the west of the city, heard the emperor was in the north, and therefore went with the excellencies and ministers to welcome him at the foot of North Mang Slope.
translations.idiomatic: before dawn he reached the west of the city, heard the emperor was in the north, and went with the excellencies and ministers to welcome him at the foot of North Mang Slope.

sentences.zh: 帝見卓將兵卒至，恐怖涕泣。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw Zhuo's troops arrive suddenly, he was terrified and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw Zhuo's troops arrive suddenly, he was terrified and wept.

sentences.zh: 群公謂卓曰：「有詔卻兵。

translations.literal: The assembled lords said to Zhuo: "There is an edict to withdraw the troops."
translations.idiomatic: The assembled lords said to Zhuo: "There is an edict ordering you to withdraw your troops."

sentences.zh: 」卓曰：「公諸人為國大臣，不能匡正王室，至使國家播蕩，何卻兵之有！

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "You gentlemen are great ministers of the state yet could not rectify the royal house, until the state was thrown into turmoil—what talk is there of withdrawing troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo said: "You gentlemen are great ministers of the state yet could not rectify the royal house until the realm was thrown into turmoil—what talk is there of withdrawing troops!"

sentences.zh: 」卓與帝語，語不可了；

translations.literal: Zhuo spoke with the emperor, but his words could not be made out;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo spoke with the emperor, but his words could not be understood;

sentences.zh: 乃更與陳留王語，問禍亂由起，王答，自初至終，無所遺失。

translations.literal: he then spoke instead with the King of Chenliu, asking whence the calamity and turmoil arose; the king answered from beginning to end without omitting anything.
translations.idiomatic: he then spoke instead with the King of Chenliu, asking whence the calamity arose; the king answered from beginning to end without omitting anything.

sentences.zh: 卓大喜，以王為賢，且為董太后所養，卓自以與太后同族，遂有廢立之意。

translations.literal: Zhuo was greatly pleased, considered the king worthy, and moreover, since the king had been raised by Empress Dowager Dong and Zhuo regarded himself as of the same clan as the empress dowager, he then conceived the intent to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was greatly pleased and considered the king worthy; moreover, since the king had been raised by Empress Dowager Dong and Zhuo regarded himself as of the same clan, he then conceived the intent to depose and enthrone.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝還宮，赦天下，改光熹為昭寧。

translations.literal: That day the emperor returned to the palace, amnestied all under Heaven, and changed Guangxi to Zhaoning.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor returned to the palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Guangxi to Zhaoning.

sentences.zh: 失傳國璽，餘璽皆得之。

translations.literal: The seal of imperial transmission was lost; the remaining seals were all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal of transmission was lost; the remaining seals were all recovered.

sentences.zh: 以丁原為執金吾。

translations.literal: Ding Yuan was made Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Yuan was appointed Bearer of the Mace.

sentences.zh: 騎都尉鮑信自泰山募兵適至，說袁紹曰：「董卓擁強兵，將有異志，今不早圖，必為所制；

translations.literal: The Commandant of Cavalry Bao Xin, having just arrived from raising troops in Taishan, urged Yuan Shao: "Dong Zhuo holds a strong army and will harbor divergent intent—if you do not plot against him early, you are sure to be controlled by him;
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavalry Bao Xin, having just arrived from raising troops in Taishan, urged Yuan Shao: "Dong Zhuo holds a strong army and harbors divergent intent—if you do not move against him early, you are sure to be controlled by him;

sentences.zh: 乃其新至疲勞，襲之，可禽也！

translations.literal: moreover, he has newly arrived and is weary—strike him and he can be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: moreover, he has newly arrived and is weary—strike him now and he can be captured!"

sentences.zh: 」紹畏卓，不敢發。

translations.literal: Shao feared Zhuo and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Shao feared Zhuo and did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 信乃引兵還泰山。

translations.literal: Xin then led his troops back to Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then led his troops back to Taishan.

sentences.zh: 董卓之入也，步騎不過三千，自嫌兵少，恐不為遠近所服，率四五日輒夜潛出軍近營，明旦，乃大陳旌鼓而還，以為西兵復至，雒中無知者。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo entered, his infantry and cavalry numbered no more than three thousand; he himself thought his troops few and feared he would not be submitted to by near and far; every four or five days he would secretly lead troops out by night to camps nearby, and at dawn would display banners and drums in great array and return, so that it was thought western troops had come again—none in Luoyang knew the truth.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo entered the capital, his infantry and cavalry numbered no more than three thousand; thinking his force too small to command respect near and far, every four or five days he would secretly lead troops out by night to nearby camps and at dawn return with banners and drums displayed in great array, so that it was thought western troops had arrived again—none in Luoyang knew the truth.

sentences.zh: 俄而進及遞苗部曲皆歸於卓，卓又陰使丁原部曲司馬五原呂布殺原而並其眾，卓兵於是大盛。

translations.literal: Before long the troops of Jin and Di Miao all came over to Zhuo; Zhuo also secretly had Ding Yuan's staff Major, Lü Bu of Wuyuan, kill Yuan and absorb his forces, and Zhuo's army thereby grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the troops of Jin and He Miao all came over to Zhuo; Zhuo also secretly had Ding Yuan's staff Major Lü Bu of Wuyuan kill Yuan and absorb his forces, and Zhuo's army thereby grew greatly.

sentences.zh: 乃諷朝廷，以久雨，策免司空劉弘而代之。

translations.literal: He then prompted the court that, because of long rains, Minister of Works Liu Hong should be removed by imperial letter and replaced by himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then prompted the court that, because of prolonged rains, Minister of Works Liu Hong should be removed by imperial letter and replaced by himself.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡邕徙朔方，會赦得還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cai Yong had been banished to Shuofang and, when an amnesty came, was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cai Yong had been banished to Shuofang and, when an amnesty came, was able to return.

sentences.zh: 五原太守王智，甫之弟也，奏蔡邕謗訕朝廷；

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, Administrator of Wuyuan and younger brother of Fu, memorialized that Cai Yong had slandered and mocked the court;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, Administrator of Wuyuan and younger brother of Fu, memorialized that Cai Yong had slandered and mocked the court;

sentences.zh: 邕遂亡命江海，積十二年，董卓聞其名而辟之，稱疾不就。

translations.literal: Yong then fled for his life to the rivers and seas; after twelve years Dong Zhuo heard his name and summoned him, but he pleaded illness and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then fled for his life to the rivers and seas; after twelve years Dong Zhuo heard his name and summoned him, but he pleaded illness and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 卓怒，詈曰：「我能族人！

translations.literal: Zhuo was angry and cursed: "I can exterminate your clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was angry and cursed: "I can exterminate your clan!"

sentences.zh: 」邕懼而應命，到，署祭酒，甚見敬重，舉高第，三日之間，周歷三台，遷為侍中。

translations.literal: Yong was afraid and obeyed the summons; when he arrived he was appointed Libationer, was greatly respected and honored, was ranked in the highest grade, and within three days passed through all Three Platforms and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was afraid and obeyed; when he arrived he was appointed Libationer, was greatly respected, was ranked in the highest grade, and within three days passed through all Three Platforms and was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 董卓謂袁紹曰：「天下之主，宜得賢明，每念靈帝，令人憤毒！

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo said to Yuan Shao: "The ruler of all under Heaven ought to be worthy and enlightened; whenever I think of Emperor Ling, it fills me with poisonous rage!
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo said to Yuan Shao: "The ruler of the realm ought to be worthy and enlightened; whenever I think of Emperor Ling, it fills me with poisonous rage!

sentences.zh: 董侯似可，今欲立之，為能勝史侯否？

translations.literal: The Marquis of Dong seems suitable; I now wish to establish him—can he surpass the Marquis of Shi?
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Dong seems suitable; I now wish to enthrone him—can he surpass the Marquis of Shi?

sentences.zh: 人有小智大癡，亦知復何如？

translations.literal: A man may have small wisdom and great foolishness—who knows how it will turn out?
translations.idiomatic: A man may have small wisdom and great foolishness—who knows how it will turn out?

sentences.zh: 為當且爾。

translations.literal: For now, let it be so.
translations.idiomatic: For now, let it be so.

sentences.zh: 劉氏種不足復遺！

translations.literal: The seed of the Liu house is not worth preserving!"
translations.idiomatic: The seed of the Liu house is not worth preserving!"

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「漢家君天下四百許年，恩澤深渥，兆民戴之。

translations.literal: Shao said: "The Han house has ruled all under Heaven for some four hundred years; its grace is deep and rich, and the myriad people uphold it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "The Han house has ruled the realm for some four hundred years; its grace is deep and rich, and the myriad people uphold it.

sentences.zh: 今上富於春秋，未有不善宣於天下。

translations.literal: The present sovereign is rich in years of youth and has shown no ill conduct proclaimed to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign is still young and has shown no ill conduct known to the realm.

sentences.zh: 公欲廢嫡立庶，恐眾不從公議也。

translations.literal: If Your Excellency wishes to depose the heir and establish the younger son, I fear the multitude will not follow your proposal."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to depose the heir and establish the younger son, I fear the multitude will not follow your proposal."

sentences.zh: 」卓按劍叱紹曰：「豎子敢然！

translations.literal: Zhuo gripped his sword and shouted at Shao: "You brat dare do this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo gripped his sword and shouted at Shao: "You brat dare speak thus!

sentences.zh: 天下之事，豈不在我！

translations.literal: Affairs of all under Heaven—are they not in my hands!
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of the realm—are they not in my hands!

sentences.zh: 我欲為之，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: What I wish to do—who dares not follow!
translations.idiomatic: What I wish to do—who dares not follow!

sentences.zh: 爾謂董卓刀為不利乎！

translations.literal: Do you think Dong Zhuo's blade is not sharp!"
translations.idiomatic: Do you think Dong Zhuo's blade is not sharp!"

sentences.zh: 」紹勃然曰：「天下健者，豈惟董公！

translations.literal: Shao flushed with anger and said: "Bold men under Heaven—are they only Lord Dong!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao flushed with anger and said: "Bold men under Heaven—are they only Lord Dong!"

sentences.zh: 」引佩刀，橫揖，逕出。

translations.literal: He drew his girdle sword, bowed with arms crossed, and went straight out.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his girdle sword, bowed with arms crossed, and went straight out.

sentences.zh: 卓以新至，見紹大家，故不敢害。

translations.literal: Zhuo, having newly arrived and seeing that Shao came from a great house, therefore did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo, having newly arrived and seeing that Shao came from a great house, did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 紹縣節於上東門，逃奔冀州。

translations.literal: Shao hung his credential staff at the Upper East Gate and fled to Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao hung his credential staff at the Upper East Gate and fled to Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸酉，卓大會百寮，奮首而言曰：「皇帝闇弱，不可以奉宗廟，為天下主。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guiyou, Zhuo convened a great assembly of the hundred officials, raised his head and spoke, saying: "The emperor is dim and weak; he cannot attend to the ancestral temples and be lord of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiyou day, Dong Zhuo convened a grand assembly of officials, threw back his head, and declared: "The emperor is feeble and inept; he cannot uphold the ancestral shrines or rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 今欲依伊尹、霍光故事，更立陳留王，何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to follow the precedents of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and install the Prince of Chenliu in his place—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I propose to follow the precedents of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and set up the Prince of Chenliu instead—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」公卿以下皆惶恐，莫敢對。

translations.literal: " From the Three Excellencies down, all were terrified and none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: " From the chief ministers downward, all were stricken with fear; not one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 卓又抗言曰：「昔霍光定策，延年按劍。

translations.literal: Zhuo again spoke defiantly, saying: "In former times Huo Guang settled the succession and Yannian laid hand on his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo spoke defiantly again: "When Huo Guang settled the succession, Yannian rested his hand on his sword.

sentences.zh: 有敢沮大議，皆以軍法從事！

translations.literal: Whoever dares obstruct this great design shall be dealt with by military law!
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who dares block this measure will face military justice!

sentences.zh: 」坐者震動，尚書盧植獨曰：「昔太甲既立不明，昌邑罪過千餘，故有廢立之事。

translations.literal: " Those seated were shaken. Alone among them Minister of the Masters of Writing Lu Zhi said: "In former times, after Tai Jia was enthroned he proved unenlightened, and the Prince of Changyi's offenses numbered more than a thousand—therefore there were depositions and installations.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembly quaked. Only Lu Zhi, Minister of the Masters of Writing, spoke up: "Long ago Tai Jia proved unfit after his accession, and the Prince of Changyi's crimes ran to more than a thousand counts—hence those depositions and installations.

sentences.zh: 今上富於春秋，行無失德，非前事之比也。

translations.literal: The present sovereign is in the prime of youth; his conduct has no lost virtue—it is not comparable to those earlier cases.
translations.idiomatic: Our present lord is still young; his conduct shows no lapse of virtue. This case is not comparable to those.

sentences.zh: 」卓大怒，罷坐。

translations.literal: " Zhuo was greatly enraged and dismissed the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo flew into a rage and adjourned the meeting.

sentences.zh: 將殺植，蔡邕為之請，議郎彭伯亦諫卓曰：「盧尚書海內大儒，人之望也。

translations.literal: He was about to kill Zhi; Cai Yong pleaded on his behalf, and Court Gentleman Peng Bo also remonstrated with Zhuo, saying: "Minister Lu is the great Confucian of the realm—the hope of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of executing Lu Zhi; Cai Yong interceded for him, and Gentleman of the Palace Peng Bo also admonished Dong Zhuo: "Minister Lu is the foremost scholar of the empire—the man in whom all place their hopes.

sentences.zh: 今先害之，天下震怖。

translations.literal: If you harm him first, all under Heaven will be shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Strike him down now and the whole realm will quake with dread.

sentences.zh: 」卓乃止，但免植官，植遂逃隱於上谷。

translations.literal: " Zhuo then stopped; he merely removed Zhi from office, and Zhi thereupon fled into seclusion in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo relented, stripped Lu Zhi of office only, and Lu Zhi fled into hiding in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 卓以廢立議示太傅袁隗，隗報如議。

translations.literal: Zhuo showed the abdication-and-installation proposal to Grand Tutor Yuan Kui, and Kui replied in accord with the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo showed the deposition proposal to Grand Tutor Yuan Kui, who assented.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，卓復會群僚於崇德前殿，遂脅太后策廢少帝，曰：「皇帝在喪，無人子之心，威儀不類人君，今廢為弘農王，立陳留王協為帝。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zhuo again convened the officials at the front hall of Chongde Palace and thereupon coerced the empress dowager to issue an edict deposing the Young Emperor, saying: "The emperor is in mourning yet lacks a son's heart; his bearing and ritual do not resemble a sovereign—now he is deposed as King of Hongnong, and the Prince of Chenliu Xie is installed as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day, Dong Zhuo reconvened the officials in the front hall of Chongde Palace and forced the empress dowager to decree the Young Emperor's deposition: "The emperor is in mourning yet shows no filial heart. His bearing is unworthy of a ruler. He is deposed as King of Hongnong, and Prince Xie of Chenliu is enthroned as emperor.

sentences.zh: 」袁隗解帝璽綬，以奉陳留王，扶弘農王下殿，北面稱臣。

translations.literal: " Yuan Kui removed the imperial seal and sash and presented them to the Prince of Chenliu; he helped the King of Hongnong down from the dais, who faced north and declared himself a subject.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Kui removed the imperial seal and sash and presented them to the Prince of Chenliu, then escorted the King of Hongnong down from the throne; the deposed emperor turned north and paid obeisance as a subject.

sentences.zh: 太后鯁涕，群臣含悲，莫敢言者。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was choked with tears; the officials bore grief within, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept until she could hardly breathe; the officials swallowed their grief, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 卓又議：「太后踧迫永樂宮，至令憂死，逆婦姑之禮。

translations.literal: Zhuo further proposed: "The empress dowager pressured and harassed the Yongle Palace until worry brought death—contrary to the rites between daughter-in-law and mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo further argued: "The empress dowager harassed the palace at Yongle until the former empress died of grief—a breach of the rites between daughter-in-law and mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 」乃遷太后於永安宮。

translations.literal: " He then moved the empress dowager to Yongan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He then relocated the empress dowager to Yongan Palace.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改昭寧為永漢。

translations.literal: He proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven and changed the era name from Zhaoning to Yonghan.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and renamed the era from Zhaoning to Yonghan.

sentences.zh: 丙子，卓鴆殺何太后，公卿以下不布服，會葬，素衣而已。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Zhuo poisoned Empress Dowager He; from the Three Excellencies down no one wore mourning garb—at the funeral they wore only plain white clothing.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day, Dong Zhuo poisoned Empress Dowager He. From the chief ministers downward, none wore proper mourning; at the burial they appeared in plain white garments only.

sentences.zh: 卓又發何苗棺，出其屍，支解節斷，棄於道邊，殺苗母舞陽君，棄屍於苑枳落中。

translations.literal: Zhuo also exhumed He Miao's coffin, took out his corpse, dismembered it joint by joint, and cast it beside the road; he killed Miao's mother Lady Wuyang and abandoned her corpse among the thorn thickets in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo also opened He Miao's coffin, pulled out the corpse, hacked it limb from limb, and dumped it by the roadside. He killed Miao's mother, Lady Wuyang, and threw her body into the thorn thickets of the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 詔除公卿以下子弟為郎，以補宦官之職，侍於殿上。

translations.literal: An edict appointed sons and younger brothers of officials from the Three Excellencies down as Gentlemen of the Palace to fill eunuch posts and attend in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed the sons of officials, from the chief ministers downward, as gentlemen of the palace to replace the eunuchs' duties and serve in the hall.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以太尉劉虞為大司馬，封襄賁侯。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Liu Yu was appointed Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day, Liu Yu, Grand Commandant, was made Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangben.

sentences.zh: 董卓自為太尉，領前將軍事，加節傳、斧鉞、虎賁，更封郿侯。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo made himself Grand Commandant, took charge of the former general's military affairs, was granted credentials, battle-axe, and Tiger Guards, and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo appointed himself Grand Commandant, assumed command of the Former General's forces, received the insignia of imperial commission—credentials, battle-axe, and Tiger Guards—and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Mei.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以太中大夫楊彪為司空。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Senior Grandee Yang Biao was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, Yang Biao, Senior Grandee, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以豫州牧黃琬為司徒。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Inspector of Yuzhou Huang Wan was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day, Huang Wan, governor of Yuzhou, was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 董卓率諸公上書，追理陳蕃、竇武及諸黨人，悉復其爵位，遣使吊祠，擢用其子孫。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo led the nobles in a memorial to reconsider Chen Fan, Dou Wu, and the various partisans, fully restoring their titles and ranks, sending envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices, and promoting their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo led the ranking officials in a memorial to reassess Chen Fan, Dou Wu, and their partisans, fully restoring their titles, dispatching envoys to mourn them at sacrifice, and promoting their descendants to office.

sentences.zh: 自六月雨至於是月。

translations.literal: From the sixth month rain continued until this month.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had fallen continuously from the sixth month until now.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙巳，葬靈思皇后。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yisi, Empress Ling Si was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on yisi day, Empress Ling Si was interred.

sentences.zh: 白波賊寇河東，董卓遣其將牛輔擊之。

translations.literal: White Wave bandits raided Hedong; Dong Zhuo sent his general Niu Fu to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: White Wave bandits invaded Hedong; Dong Zhuo sent his general Niu Fu against them.

sentences.zh: 初，南單于於扶羅既立，國人殺其父者遂叛，共立須卜骨都侯為單于。

translations.literal: Initially, after the Southern Chanyu Yufuluo had been installed, those of his countrymen who had killed his father then rebelled and together installed Xubu Guduhou as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Southern Chanyu Yufuluo had been enthroned, those among his people who had killed his father rebelled and jointly set up Xubu Guduhou as chanyu.

sentences.zh: 於扶羅指闕自訟。

translations.literal: Yufuluo pointed to the palace gate and pleaded his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Yufuluo went to the imperial gate to plead his case in person.

sentences.zh: 會靈帝崩，天下大亂，於扶羅將數千騎與白波賊合兵寇郡縣。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Ling died and all under Heaven fell into great disorder; Yufuluo led several thousand horsemen to join forces with the White Wave bandits and raid commanderies and districts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ling died and the realm plunged into chaos, Yufuluo led several thousand horsemen to join the White Wave bandits and ravage the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 時民皆保聚，鈔掠無利，而兵遂挫傷。

translations.literal: At the time the people all gathered for protection, so plunder brought no profit, and the troops were defeated and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The populace had banded together in fortified settlements, yielding no profit from raids, and the allied forces were beaten and battered.

sentences.zh: 復欲歸國，國人不受，乃止河東平陽。

translations.literal: He again wished to return to his state, but his countrymen would not receive him, so he halted at Pingyang in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yufuluo tried to return home, but his people refused him; he halted at Pingyang in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 須卜骨都侯為單于一年而死，南庭遂虛其位，以老王行國事。

translations.literal: Xubu Guduhou had been Chanyu one year and died; the Southern Court thereupon left the seat vacant and had the old king conduct state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xubu Guduhou ruled one year and died; the Southern Court left the throne vacant and entrusted governance to the elder king.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以董卓為相國，贊拜不名，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Dong Zhuo was made Chancellor of State, addressed without naming him, permitted to enter court without hurrying, and allowed sword and shoes on the palace dais.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Dong Zhuo was appointed Chancellor of State, with the privilege of being addressed without naming his person, entering court without hastening, and wearing sword and shoes on the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊戌，以司徒黃琬為太尉，司空楊彪為司徒，光祿勳荀爽為司空。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuxu, Minister over the Masses Huang Wan was made Grand Commandant, Minister of Works Yang Biao was made Minister over the Masses, and Director of the Masters of the Imperial Household Xun Shuang was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuxu day, Huang Wan moved from Minister over the Masses to Grand Commandant; Yang Biao, from Minister of Works to Minister over the Masses; and Xun Shuang, Director of the Masters of the Imperial Household, became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書武威周毖、城門校尉汝南伍瓊，說董卓矯桓、靈之政，擢用天下名士以收眾望，卓從之，命毖、瓊與尚書鄭泰、長史何顒等沙汰穢惡，顯拔幽滯。

translations.literal: Initially, Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhou Bi of Wuwei and Colonel of the City Gates Wu Qiong of Runan persuaded Dong Zhuo to correct the policies of Huan and Ling, promote famous scholars from all under Heaven to win popular esteem; Zhuo followed this, ordering Bi, Qiong, Minister Zheng Tai, Chief Clerk He Yong, and others to sift out the corrupt and wicked and clearly elevate those in obscurity and stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhou Bi of Wuwei, Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Wu Qiong of Runan, Colonel of the City Gates, urged Dong Zhuo to reverse the policies of Emperors Huan and Ling and appoint renowned scholars across the realm to win public favor. Dong Zhuo agreed and ordered Bi, Qiong, Zheng Tai, He Yong, and others to purge corruption and elevate neglected talent.

sentences.zh: 於是征處士荀爽、陳紀、韓融、申屠蟠。

translations.literal: Thereupon recluses Xun Shuang, Chen Ji, Han Rong, and Shentu Pan were summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Recluses Xun Shuang, Chen Ji, Han Rong, and Shentu Pan were summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 復就拜爽平原相，行至宛陵，遷光祿勳，視事三日，進拜司空。

translations.literal: Shuang was again appointed on the spot as Chancellor of Pingyuan; when he reached Wanling he was transferred to Director of the Masters of the Imperial Household; after three days in office he was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Shuang was promptly appointed chancellor of Pingyuan; reaching Wanling, he was made Director of the Masters of the Imperial Household; after three days in that post he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 自被征命及登台司，凡九十三日。

translations.literal: From receiving the summons until reaching the highest ministries—in all, ninety-three days.
translations.idiomatic: From summons to the highest office—ninety-three days in all.

sentences.zh: 又以紀為五官中郎將，融為大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Ji was also made General of the Palace Gate with Five Titles, and Rong was made Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ji was made General of the Five Offices, and Han Rong became Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 紀，寔之子；

translations.literal: Ji was the son of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ji was the son of Chen Shi.

sentences.zh: 融，韶之子也。

translations.literal: Rong was the son of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Rong was the son of Han Shao.

sentences.zh: 爽等皆畏卓之暴，無敢不至。

translations.literal: Shuang and the others all feared Zhuo's ferocity and none dared not come.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Shuang and the others, fearing Dong Zhuo's brutality, all came—none dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 獨申屠蟠得征書，人勸之行，蟠笑而不答，卓終不能屈，年七十餘，以壽終。

translations.literal: Only Shentu Pan received the summons; people urged him to go, but Pan smiled and did not answer; Zhuo in the end could not bend him; in his seventies and more he died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shentu Pan, when summoned, was urged to go; he smiled and gave no answer. Dong Zhuo never broke him. He lived past seventy and died a natural death.

sentences.zh: 卓又以尚書韓馥為冀州牧，侍中劉岱為兗州刺史，陳留孔胄為豫州刺史，東平張邈為陳留太守，穎川張咨為南陽太守。

translations.literal: Zhuo also made Minister Han Fu Inspector of Jizhou, Palace Attendant Liu Dai Inspector of Yanzhou, Kong Zhou of Chenliu Inspector of Yuzhou, Zhang Miao of Dongping Administrator of Chenliu, and Zhang Zi of Yingchuan Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo also appointed Han Fu governor of Jizhou, Liu Dai governor of Yanzhou, Kong Zhou of Chenliu governor of Yuzhou, Zhang Miao of Dongping administrator of Chenliu, and Zhang Zi of Yingchuan administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 卓所親愛，並不處顯職，但將校而已。

translations.literal: Those whom Zhuo personally favored were none placed in conspicuous offices—they were only generals and commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's personal favorites held no prominent civil posts—they served only as military officers.

sentences.zh: 詔除光熹、昭寧、永漢三號。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the three era names Guangxi, Zhaoning, and Yonghan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the three short-lived era names Guangxi, Zhaoning, and Yonghan.

sentences.zh: 董卓性殘忍，一旦專政，據有國家甲兵、珍寶，威震天下，所願無極，語賓客曰：「我相，貴無上也！

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo's nature was cruel and ruthless; once he held sole power he possessed the state's armor and troops and treasures, his might shook all under Heaven, his desires knew no limit; he said to his guests: "As chancellor, my nobility has no superior!
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was cruel by nature. Once he held sole power, he commanded the realm's armies and hoarded its treasures; his might shook the world and his ambitions knew no bound. He told his retainers: "As chancellor, no rank stands above mine!

sentences.zh: 」侍御史擾龍宗詣卓白事，不解劍，立撾殺之。

translations.literal: " Attendant Imperial Censor Rao Longzong came to Zhuo to report affairs and did not remove his sword; he was beaten to death on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " The attendant censor Rao Longzong came to report to Dong Zhuo and failed to remove his sword; Dong Zhuo had him beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 是時，洛中貴戚，室第相望，金帛財產，家家充積，卓縱放兵士，突其廬舍，剽虜資物，妻略婦女，不避貴賤。

translations.literal: At this time in Luoyang the noble kin, their mansions lining the streets, gold and silk and goods piled in every house; Zhuo unleashed his soldiers to break into their dwellings, plunder goods, seize women as wives, sparing neither noble nor base.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang the aristocracy lived in mansions side by side, their houses heaped with gold and treasure. Dong Zhuo turned his soldiers loose to storm their homes, loot their wealth, and seize their women, sparing neither high nor low.

sentences.zh: 人情崩恐，不保朝夕。

translations.literal: People's hearts collapsed in terror; none could be sure of the morrow.
translations.idiomatic: Panic seized the populace; no one could count on surviving from one day to the next.

sentences.zh: 卓購求袁紹急，周毖、伍瓊說卓曰：「夫廢立大事，非常人所及。

translations.literal: Zhuo urgently sought Yuan Shao with a bounty; Zhou Bi and Wu Qiong said to Zhuo: "The great affair of deposition and installation lies beyond what ordinary men can grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo urgently sought Yuan Shao with a price on his head. Zhou Bi and Wu Qiong urged him: "Deposing and installing an emperor is an extraordinary deed—beyond what ordinary men can bear.

sentences.zh: 袁紹不達大體，恐懼出奔，非有它志。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao did not comprehend the great design; in fear he fled—he has no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao failed to grasp the larger design and fled in fear; he harbors no other design.

sentences.zh: 今急購之，勢必為變。

translations.literal: If you urgently hunt him now, the situation will surely turn to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Hunt him down now and you will surely provoke rebellion.

sentences.zh: 袁氏樹恩四世，門生故吏遍於天下，若收豪傑以聚徒眾，英雄因之而起，則山東非公之有也。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan has planted favor over four generations; their students and former subordinates fill all under Heaven—if they gather heroes and assemble followers, heroes will rise in response, and then the lands east of the mountains will not be yours.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan family has cultivated ties for four generations; their protégés and former subordinates span the realm. Gather heroes to his banner and the east will no longer be yours.

sentences.zh: 不如赦之，拜一郡守，紹喜於免罪，必無患矣。

translations.literal: Better to pardon him and appoint him to a prefecture; Shao will rejoice at escaping punishment and will surely be without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Better pardon him and appoint him to a commandery post; Yuan Shao, grateful to escape punishment, will pose no threat.

sentences.zh: 」卓以為然，乃即拜紹勃海太守，封邟鄉侯。

translations.literal: " Zhuo thought this right and thereupon promptly appointed Shao Administrator of Bohai and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Angiang.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo agreed and immediately made Yuan Shao administrator of Bohai and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Angiang.

sentences.zh: 又以袁術為後將軍，曹操為驍騎校尉。

translations.literal: He also made Yuan Shu General of the Rear and Cao Cao Colonel of Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Yuan Shu General of the Rear and Cao Cao Colonel of Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 術畏卓，出奔南陽。

translations.literal: Shu feared Zhuo and fled to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, fearing Dong Zhuo, fled to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 操變易姓名，間行東歸，過中牟，為亭長所疑，執詣縣。

translations.literal: Cao altered his name, traveled secretly eastward, passed through Zhongmou, was suspected by a station chief, seized and taken to the district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao changed his identity and made his way east by side roads; passing through Zhongmou, a station chief grew suspicious and had him seized and taken to the county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 時縣已被卓書，唯功曹心知是操，以世方亂，不宜拘天下雄俊，因白令釋之。

translations.literal: At the time the district had already received Zhuo's letter; only the Master of Records knew in his heart it was Cao—since the age was in disorder, one ought not detain the realm's heroic talents, so he informed the magistrate to release him.
translations.idiomatic: The county had already received Dong Zhuo's wanted notice, but the chief clerk alone recognized Cao Cao. With the realm in turmoil, he argued, one must not imprison a man of heroic stature—and persuaded the magistrate to release him.

sentences.zh: 操至陳留，散家財，合兵得五千人。

translations.literal: Cao reached Chenliu, dispersed his family's wealth, and gathered troops numbering five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Chenliu, Cao Cao spent his family's fortune and raised a force of five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是時，豪傑多欲起兵討卓者，袁紹在勃海，冀州牧韓馥遣數部從事守之，不得動搖。

translations.literal: At this time many heroes wished to raise troops against Zhuo; Yuan Shao was in Bohai, and Inspector of Jizhou Han Fu sent several department clerks to guard him—he could not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Many champions wished to raise armies against Dong Zhuo, but Yuan Shao, in Bohai, was watched by Han Fu's deputies and could not move.

sentences.zh: 東郡太守橋瑁，詐作京師三公移書與州郡，陳卓罪惡，云：「見逼迫，無以自救，企望義兵，解國患難。

translations.literal: Administrator of Dongjun Qiao Mao forged a dispatch from the Three Excellencies of the capital to the provinces and commanderies, setting forth Zhuo's crimes, saying: "We are under coercion and have no means to save ourselves; we look to righteous armies to resolve the state's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Mao, administrator of Dong commandery, forged a letter purporting to come from the Three Excellencies in the capital to the provinces and commanderies, denouncing Dong Zhuo's crimes: "We are coerced and powerless. We look to righteous armies to deliver the state from calamity.

sentences.zh: 」馥得移，請諸從事問曰：「今當助袁氏邪，助董氏邪？

translations.literal: " Fu received the dispatch and invited the various clerks to ask: "Now should we aid the Yuan clan or aid the Dong clan?
translations.idiomatic: " Han Fu received the letter and asked his staff: "Should we aid the Yuans or aid Dong Zhuo?

sentences.zh: 」治中從事劉子惠曰：「今興兵為國，何謂袁、董！

translations.literal: " Clerk for All Affairs Liu Zihui said: "Now we raise troops for the state—what talk of Yuan or Dong!
translations.idiomatic: " Chief clerk Liu Zihui replied: "We raise arms for the state—what has this to do with Yuan or Dong!

sentences.zh: 」馥有慚色。

translations.literal: " Fu showed a shamefaced look.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Fu flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 子惠復言：「兵者凶事，不可為首。

translations.literal: Zihui further said: "War is an ill-omened affair; one must not take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zihui went on: "War is an ill omen; we must not strike first.

sentences.zh: 今宜往視他州，有發動者，然後和之。

translations.literal: Now we ought to go observe other provinces—when some have risen, then join them in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Let us watch the other provinces; when someone else moves, we join in.

sentences.zh: 冀州於他州不為弱也，他人功未有在冀州之右者也。

translations.literal: Jizhou is not weak compared to other provinces; others' achievement has none that surpasses Jizhou's.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou is no weaker than its neighbors, and no other province can claim greater merit than ours.

sentences.zh: 」馥然之。

translations.literal: " Fu assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Fu agreed.

sentences.zh: 馥乃作書與紹，道卓之惡，聽其舉兵。

translations.literal: Fu then wrote to Shao, recounting Zhuo's evil deeds, and permitted him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu wrote to Yuan Shao recounting Dong Zhuo's crimes and gave him leave to raise his army.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，關東州郡皆起兵以討董卓，推渤海太守袁紹為盟主。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the provinces and commanderies east of the Pass all raised troops to attack Dong Zhuo, recommending Yuan Shao, Administrator of Bohai, as alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, the eastern provinces and commanderies rose against Dong Zhuo and chose Yuan Shao, administrator of Bohai, as coalition chief.

sentences.zh: 紹自號車騎將軍，諸將皆板授官號。

translations.literal: Shao styled himself General of Cavalry and Chariots; the various generals all received offices inscribed on wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry; the other commanders confirmed one another's ranks on wooden tablets.

sentences.zh: 紹與河內太守王匡屯河內，冀州牧韓馥留鄴，給其軍糧，豫州刺史孔胄屯穎川，兗州刺史劉岱、陳留太守張邈、邈弟廣陵太守超、東郡太守橋瑁、山陽太守袁遺、濟北相鮑信與曹操俱屯酸棗，後將軍袁術屯魯陽，眾名數萬。

translations.literal: Shao with Administrator of Henei Wang Kuang encamped at Henei; Inspector of Jizhou Han Fu remained at Ye and supplied their army grain; Inspector of Yuzhou Kong Zhou encamped at Yingchuan; Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Dai, Administrator of Chenliu Zhang Miao, Miao's younger brother Administrator of Guangling Chao, Administrator of Dongjun Qiao Mao, Administrator of Shanyang Yuan Yi, Chancellor of Jibei Bao Xin with Cao Cao together encamped at Suanzao; General of the Rear Yuan Shu encamped at Luyang—forces in name numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Wang Kuang, administrator of Henei, camped at Henei; Han Fu stayed at Ye to provision the army; Kong Zhou held Yingchuan; Liu Dai of Yanzhou, Zhang Miao of Chenliu, Zhang Miao's brother Zhang Chao at Guangling, Qiao Mao of Dong commandery, Yuan Yi of Shanyang, Bao Xin of Jibei, and Cao Cao massed at Suanzao; Yuan Shu held Luyang. On paper their forces numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 豪傑多歸心袁紹者，鮑信獨謂曹操曰：「夫略不世出，能撥亂反正者，君也。

translations.literal: Many heroes inclined their hearts to Yuan Shao; Bao Xin alone said to Cao: "A grand design appears but once in an age; one who can set chaos aright and restore order—you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Most champions rallied to Yuan Shao, but Bao Xin told Cao Cao alone: "A statesman of grand vision appears once in an age. The man who can set the realm right after chaos—that is you.

sentences.zh: 苟非其人，雖強必斃。

translations.literal: If it is not the right person, though strong he must perish.
translations.idiomatic: Without the right leader, even the strongest coalition must fail.

sentences.zh: 君殆天之所啟乎！

translations.literal: My lord, are you not perhaps heaven's chosen one!
translations.idiomatic: Are you not heaven's chosen?

sentences.zh: 辛亥，赦天下。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，董卓使郎中令李儒鴆殺弘農王辯。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Dong Zhuo had Director of the Masters of the Imperial Household Li Ru poison the King of Hongnong Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day, Dong Zhuo had Li Ru, Director of the Masters of the Imperial Household, poison the King of Hongnong, Liu Bian.

sentences.zh: 卓議大發兵以討山東。

translations.literal: Zhuo deliberated on greatly raising troops to attack the east.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo debated mobilizing a massive army to crush the eastern coalition.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄭泰曰：「夫政在德，不在眾也。

translations.literal: Minister Zheng Tai said: "Government lies in virtue, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Tai said: "Governance rests on virtue, not on numbers.

sentences.zh: 」卓不悅曰：「如卿此言，兵為無用邪！

translations.literal: " Zhuo, displeased, said: "By your words, are troops useless!
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo bristled: "By that logic, armies are useless!

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「非謂其然也，以為山東不足加大兵耳。

translations.literal: " Tai said: "I do not mean it is so; I hold that the east is not worth applying great troops to.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Tai replied: "That is not what I mean. The east is not worth a major campaign.

sentences.zh: 明公出自西州，少為將帥，閑習軍事。

translations.literal: Your Grace comes from the western provinces, were from youth a commander, and are practiced in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: You hail from the western frontier and have commanded armies since youth; warfare is second nature to you.

sentences.zh: 袁本初公卿子弟，生處京師，張孟卓東平長者，坐不窺堂，孔公緒清談高論，噓枯吹生。

translations.literal: Yuan Benchu is a son of grandees, born and raised in the capital; Zhang Mengzhuo is an elder of Dongping—sits without glancing beyond the hall; Kong Gongxu engages in pure talk and lofty discourse, boasting of reviving the withered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is a pampered court scion raised in the capital. Zhang Miao is a respectable gentleman of Dongping who never so much as glanced past his own hall. Kong Zhou traffics in lofty chatter and idle boasts of reviving the withered.

sentences.zh: 並無軍旅之才，臨鋒決敵，非公之儔也。

translations.literal: None has talent for armies and campaigns; facing the blades and deciding the foe—they are no match for Your Grace.
translations.idiomatic: None of them knows war. In a clash of arms they are no match for you.

sentences.zh: 況王爵不加，尊卑無序，若恃眾怙力，將各棋峙以觀成敗，不肯同心共膽，與齊進退也。

translations.literal: Moreover, kingly titles are not bestowed and high and low are without order—if they rely on numbers and lean on strength, each will stand like chess pieces watching success or failure, unwilling to unite hearts and guts, advance and retreat together.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they lack proper rank and clear hierarchy. Trusting only their numbers, each will hold his ground like pieces on a board, waiting to see who wins—unwilling to share one mind or move as one.

sentences.zh: 且山東承平日久，民不習戰；

translations.literal: Moreover the east has enjoyed peace long; the people are unpracticed in war;
translations.idiomatic: The east has known peace for generations; its people are unused to fighting;

sentences.zh: 關西頃遭羌寇，婦女皆能挾弓而鬥，天下所畏者，無若並、涼之人與羌、胡義從；

translations.literal: west of the Pass recently suffered Qiang raids—even women can grasp bow and fight; what all under Heaven fears, nothing surpasses the men of Bing and Liang and the volunteer bands of Qiang and Hu;
translations.idiomatic: while the northwest has weathered Qiang raids—even women there can draw a bow and fight. The fiercest fighters under heaven are the men of Bing and Liang and their Qiang and non-Chinese allies.

sentences.zh: 而明公擁之以為爪牙，譬猶驅虎兕以赴犬羊，鼓烈風以掃枯葉，誰敢御之！

translations.literal: yet Your Grace holds them as claws and fangs—like driving tigers and rhinoceroses against dogs and sheep, raising a fierce wind to sweep dry leaves—who would dare resist!
translations.idiomatic: You command them as your claws and fangs. It is like setting tigers and rhinos on sheep, or unleashing a gale to scatter dead leaves. Who could stand against you!

sentences.zh: 無事徵兵以驚天下，使患役之民相聚為非，棄德恃眾，自虧威重也。

translations.literal: To raise troops without cause and alarm all under Heaven, causing the people weary of corvée to gather in wrongdoing—abandoning virtue and relying on numbers—you yourself diminish your weight of awe.
translations.idiomatic: To mobilize without cause would alarm the realm, drive the overburdened into rebellion, and trade moral authority for brute force—you would diminish your own prestige.

sentences.zh: 」卓乃悅。

translations.literal: " Zhuo was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo was pleased.

sentences.zh: 董卓以山東兵盛，欲遷都以避之，公卿皆不欲而莫敢言。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo, because eastern troops were strong, wished to move the capital to avoid them; the Three Excellencies all disliked it yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: With the eastern armies swelling, Dong Zhuo wished to move the capital to escape them. The chief ministers opposed it but dared not say so.

sentences.zh: 卓表河南尹朱俊為太僕以為己副，使者召拜，俊辭，不肯受，因曰：「國家西遷，必孤天下之望，以成山東之釁，臣不知其可也。

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized that Administrator of Henan Zhu Jun be made Grand Master of Ceremonies as his deputy; the envoy came to summon and invest him; Jun declined and would not accept, saying: "If the state moves west, it will surely isolate the hopes of all under Heaven and complete the eastern rebellion—I do not know that it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo recommended Zhu Jun, Intendant of Henan, as Grand Master of Ceremonies and his deputy. When the envoy came to invest him, Zhu Jun refused and said: "Moving the capital westward will alienate the hopes of the realm and give the eastern coalition its pretext. I cannot see how this serves the state.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「召君受拜而君拒之，不問徙事而君陳之，何也？

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "We summoned you to receive investiture yet you refuse; you were not asked about the move yet you set it forth—why?
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said: "You were summoned to accept appointment, yet you refuse—and without being asked about the move, you lecture on it. Why?

sentences.zh: 」俊曰：「副相國，非臣所堪也；

translations.literal: " Jun said: "Deputy to the Chancellor of State—I am not equal to it;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Jun said: "Serving as your deputy is more than I can bear;

sentences.zh: 遷都非計，事所急也。

translations.literal: moving the capital is no plan—it is what the matter urgently needs.
translations.idiomatic: and moving the capital is a bad plan—the urgent matter is exactly that.

sentences.zh: 辭所不堪，言其所急，臣之宜也。

translations.literal: to decline what one cannot bear, to speak what is urgent—this is what a minister should do.
translations.idiomatic: To refuse what one cannot accept and speak to what is pressing—that is a minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 」由是止不為副。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stopped and did not make him deputy.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Dong Zhuo dropped the appointment and did not make Zhu Jun his deputy.

sentences.zh: 卓大會公卿議，曰：「高祖都關中，十有一世，光武宮雒陽，於今亦十一世矣。

translations.literal: Zhuo held a great assembly of the Three Excellencies and ministers to discuss, saying: "Gaozu made his capital in Guanzhong for eleven generations; Guangwu made his court at Luoyang—and to this day it has also been eleven generations.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo convened the chief ministers and said: "The Founder made Guanzhong his capital for eleven generations; Emperor Guangwu established his court at Luoyang—and that line, too, has now run eleven generations.

sentences.zh: 案《石包讖》，宜徙都長安，以應天人之意。

translations.literal: According to the Stone Bundle Prophecy, we ought to move the capital to Chang'an, to accord with the intent of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: The Stone Bundle Prophecy says we should move the capital to Chang'an, to answer the will of Heaven and the people.

sentences.zh: 」百官皆默然。

translations.literal: " All the officials were silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Every official in the hall fell silent.

sentences.zh: 司徒楊彪曰：「移都改制，天下大事，故盤庚遷亳，殷民胥怨。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yang Biao said: "Moving the capital and changing institutions is a great affair of all under Heaven—thus when Pan Geng moved to Bo, the people of Yin all resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Yang Biao said: "Relocating the capital and remaking the state is a matter of empire-wide consequence. When Pan Geng moved his capital to Bo, the people of Yin murmured against him.

sentences.zh: 昔關中遭王莽殘破，故光武更都雒邑，歷年已久，百姓安樂。

translations.literal: Formerly Guanzhong suffered ruin at Wang Mang's hands; therefore Guangwu changed the capital to Luoyi. Many years have passed, and the common people are settled and content.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was devastated under Wang Mang, which is why Guangwu moved the court to Luoyang. Generations have passed since then, and the people have grown secure and prosperous.

sentences.zh: 今無故捐宗廟，棄園陵，恐百姓驚動，必有糜沸之亂。

translations.literal: Now, without cause, to abandon the ancestral temples and cast aside the imperial tombs—I fear the people will be shaken, and there will surely be turmoil boiling like porridge.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the ancestral temples and imperial tombs without cause will terrify the people. You will invite chaos that seethes across the land.

sentences.zh: 《石包讖》，妖邪之書，豈可信用！

translations.literal: The Stone Bundle Prophecy is a book of demonic perversity—how can it be trusted and used!
translations.idiomatic: The Stone Bundle Prophecy is a work of sorcery and heresy. How can you put faith in it?

sentences.zh: 」卓曰：「關中肥饒，故秦得併吞六國。

translations.literal: " Zhuo said: "Guanzhong is rich and fertile—thus Qin was able to swallow and merge the Six States.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo said: "Guanzhong is rich and fertile. That is how Qin conquered the Six States.

sentences.zh: 且隴石材木自出，杜陵有武帝陶灶，並功營之，可使一朝而辦。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Longxi stone and timber come forth of themselves; at Duling there is Emperor Wu's pottery kiln—working together to build, it can be finished in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi yields stone and timber without effort. At Duling stands Emperor Wu's pottery kiln. If we mobilize labor on both fronts, the new capital can be raised in a single day.

sentences.zh: 百姓何足與議！

translations.literal: What are the common people worth discussing with!
translations.idiomatic: The common people are not worth consulting!

sentences.zh: 若有前卻，我以大兵驅之，可令詣滄海。

translations.literal: If any hesitate or fall back, I will drive them with a great army and can make them go as far as the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone resists, I will drive them with my armies all the way to the sea.

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「天下動之至易，安之甚難，惟明公慮焉！

translations.literal: " Biao said: "To set all under Heaven in motion is very easy; to settle it is very hard—may Your Excellency consider this!
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Biao said: "It is easy to throw the realm into turmoil and hard indeed to restore peace. I beg Your Excellency to weigh that carefully.

sentences.zh: 」卓作色曰：「公欲沮國計邪！

translations.literal: " Zhuo changed color and said: "Sir, do you wish to obstruct the state's plan!
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo's face darkened. "Do you mean to block the state's plan?

sentences.zh: 」太尉黃琬曰：「此國之大事，楊公之言得無可思？

translations.literal: " Grand Commandant Huang Wan said: "This is a great affair of the state—is there not something in Master Yang's words worth pondering?
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Commandant Huang Wan said: "This concerns the fate of the state. Is there not something in what Master Yang has said that deserves reflection?

sentences.zh: 」卓不答。

translations.literal: " Zhuo did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo made no answer.

sentences.zh: 司空荀爽見卓意壯，恐害彪等，因從容言曰：「相國豈樂此邪！

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xun Shuang, seeing Zhuo's resolve strong, feared harm to Biao and the others; he therefore spoke at ease, saying: "Chancellor of State, do you take pleasure in this!
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xun Shuang saw that Dong Zhuo's mind was set and feared for Yang Biao and the others. He spoke calmly: "Chancellor, do you truly relish this course?

sentences.zh: 山東兵起，非一日可禁，故當遷以圖之，此秦、漢之勢也。

translations.literal: Eastern troops have risen—they cannot be stopped in a single day; therefore one ought to move the capital to scheme against them. This is the strategic posture of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern armies cannot be crushed in a day. Moving the capital is a stratagem against them—the same logic that governed Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 」卓意小解。

translations.literal: " Zhuo's intent eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo's anger softened a little.

sentences.zh: 琬退，又為駁議。

translations.literal: Wan withdrew, then again submitted a rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan withdrew, then submitted another memorial opposing the move.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，卓以災異奏免琬、彪等，以光祿勳趙謙為太尉，太僕王允為司徒城門校尉伍瓊、督軍校尉周毖固諫遷都，卓大怒曰：「卓初入朝，二君勸用善士，故卓相從。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yihai, Zhuo memorialized on account of calamities and omens to dismiss Wan, Biao, and others; he made Minister of the Imperial Clan Zhao Qian Grand Commandant and Grand Master of Ceremonies Wang Yun Minister over the Masses. Colonel of the City Gates Wu Qiong and Colonel who Supervises the Army Zhou Bi firmly remonstrated against moving the capital. Zhuo was greatly angered and said: "When Zhuo first entered court, you two gentlemen urged employing good men, so Zhuo followed you.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day yihai, Dong Zhuo cited omens and disasters to have Huang Wan, Yang Biao, and others removed from office. He appointed Zhao Qian, Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Commandant, and Wang Yun, Grand Master of Ceremonies, Minister over the Masses. Colonel of the City Gates Wu Qiong and Colonel who Supervises the Army Zhou Bi pressed their opposition to moving the capital. Dong Zhuo flew into a rage and said: "When I first came to court, you two urged me to employ worthy men, and I followed your counsel.

sentences.zh: 而諸君到官，舉兵相圖，此二君賣卓，卓何用相負！

translations.literal: Yet when you gentlemen took office, you raised troops and plotted against one another—this is you two gentlemen selling Zhuo out. Why should Zhuo still trust you!
translations.idiomatic: Yet once in office you took up arms against one another. You betrayed me—why should I still owe you any loyalty?

sentences.zh: 」庚辰，收瓊、毖，斬之。

translations.literal: " On the day gengchen, he arrested Qiong and Bi and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day gengchen he arrested Wu Qiong and Zhou Bi and executed them.

sentences.zh: 楊彪、黃琬恐懼，詣卓謝，卓亦悔殺瓊、毖，乃復表彪、琬為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yang Biao and Huang Wan, in fear, went to Zhuo to apologize. Zhuo also regretted killing Qiong and Bi, and thereupon again memorialized to make Biao and Wan Ministers of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao and Huang Wan, terrified, went to Dong Zhuo to apologize. Dong Zhuo also regretted killing Wu Qiong and Zhou Bi, and memorialized to restore Yang Biao and Huang Wan as Ministers of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 卓征京兆尹蓋勳為議郎，時左將軍皇甫嵩將兵三萬屯扶風。

translations.literal: Zhuo summoned Intendant of Jingzhao Gai Xun to be Gentleman Consultant. At the time Left General Huangfu Song commanded thirty thousand troops stationed at Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo summoned Gai Xun, Intendant of Jingzhao, to serve as Gentleman Consultant. Meanwhile Left General Huangfu Song held Fufeng with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 勳密與嵩謀討卓。

translations.literal: Xun secretly plotted with Song to attack Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Xun secretly plotted with Huangfu Song to overthrow Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 會卓亦征嵩為城門校尉，嵩長史梁衍說嵩曰：「董卓寇掠京邑，廢立從意，今征將軍，大則危禍，小則困辱。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhuo also summoned Song to be Colonel of the City Gates. Song's Chief Clerk Liang Yan urged Song, saying: "Dong Zhuo plunders and raids the capital region, deposing and enthroning at will. Now he summons the General—in the great case, peril and disaster; in the small, hardship and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Dong Zhuo also summoned Huangfu Song to be Colonel of the City Gates. His chief clerk Liang Yan urged him: "Dong Zhuo ravages the capital, deposing and enthroning emperors at whim. If you obey this summons, you face ruin at best and humiliation at worst.

sentences.zh: 今及卓在雒陽，天子來西，以將軍之眾迎接至尊，奉令討逆，徵兵群帥，袁氏逼其東，將軍迫其西，此成禽也！

translations.literal: Now, while Zhuo is still in Luoyang and the Son of Heaven is coming west, with the General's host welcome the Supreme One, receive the command to punish the rebel, summon troops from the commanders—Yuan's clan pressing him from the east, the General pressing from the west: this is a case where he can be captured!
translations.idiomatic: Strike now, while Dong Zhuo is still in Luoyang and the emperor is moving west. With your army receive the Son of Heaven, take his mandate to punish the traitor, and rally the other commanders. The Yuan clan will press him from the east and you from the west—he will be yours for the taking!

sentences.zh: 」嵩不從，遂就征。

translations.literal: " Song did not follow this, and thereupon went to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: " Huangfu Song would not listen and went to obey the summons.

sentences.zh: 勳以眾弱不能獨立，亦還京師。

translations.literal: Xun, because his forces were few and weak and he could not stand alone, also returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Xun, too weak to act alone, returned to the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 卓以勳為直騎校尉。

translations.literal: Zhuo made Xun Colonel of the Direct Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo appointed Gai Xun Colonel of the Direct Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 河南尹朱俊為卓陳軍事，卓折俊曰：「我百戰百勝，決之於心，卿勿妄說，且污我刀！

translations.literal: Intendant of Henan Zhu Jun set forth military plans for Zhuo. Zhuo cut off Jun, saying: "I am victorious in a hundred battles and decide in my heart—do not speak rashly, lest you stain my blade!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun, Intendant of Henan, offered military counsel to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo cut him off: "I win every battle I fight and decide everything in my own mind. Do not speak nonsense—or you will stain my blade.

sentences.zh: 」蓋勳曰：「昔武丁之明，猶求箴諫，況如卿者，而欲杜人之口乎！

translations.literal: " Gai Xun said: "In former times, even in King Wu Ding's enlightenment, he still sought admonition and remonstrance—how much more one like you, yet wishing to stop people's mouths!
translations.idiomatic: " Gai Xun said: "Even King Wu Ding in his wisdom sought honest counsel. How much more should a man in your position—and yet you would silence every mouth?

sentences.zh: 」卓乃謝之。

translations.literal: " Zhuo thereupon apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhuo apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 卓遣軍至陽城，值民會於社下，悉就斬之，駕其車重，載其婦女，以頭系車轅，歌呼還雒，雲攻賊大獲。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent troops to Yangcheng. They came upon the people assembled below the altar of the soil god and beheaded them all on the spot. They drove off their carts and baggage, loaded their women, tied heads to the cart shafts, and singing and shouting returned to Luoyang, claiming a great capture in attacking bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent troops to Yangcheng. They found villagers gathered at the altar of the soil god and slaughtered them all. They seized their carts and goods, took their women, tied severed heads to the cart shafts, and marched back to Luoyang singing and shouting that they had won a great victory over bandits.

sentences.zh: 卓焚燒其頭，以婦女與甲兵為婢妾。

translations.literal: Zhuo burned their heads and gave the women to armored soldiers as maids and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo burned the heads and distributed the captive women among his soldiers as servants and concubines.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，車駕西遷。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, the imperial carriage moved west.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai the emperor's procession set out westward.

sentences.zh: 董卓收諸富室，以罪惡誅之，沒入其財物，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo seized the wealthy households, executed them on charges of crime, and confiscated their goods. The dead could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo seized wealthy families, executed them on trumped-up charges, and confiscated their property. The dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 悉驅徙其餘民數百萬口於長安。

translations.literal: He drove and relocated all the remaining people—several million mouths—to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He drove several million of the remaining populace toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 步騎驅蹙，更相蹈藉，飢餓寇掠，積屍盈路。

translations.literal: Infantry and cavalry drove and crowded them; they trampled one another in turn; hunger and bandit raids piled corpses until the roads were full.
translations.idiomatic: Foot soldiers and horsemen harried them forward. They trampled one another, starved, and were preyed upon by bandits until the roads were heaped with corpses.

sentences.zh: 卓自留屯畢圭苑中，悉燒宮廟，官府、居家，二百里內，室屋蕩盡，無復雞犬。

translations.literal: Zhuo himself remained encamped in Bigui Park and burned all palaces and temples, government offices and private homes. Within two hundred li, dwellings were swept clean—no cock or dog remained.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo himself stayed encamped in Bigui Park and burned palaces, temples, government offices, and private homes. For two hundred li around, every building was leveled—not a cock or dog was left alive.

sentences.zh: 又使呂布發諸帝陵及公卿以下塚墓，收其珍寶。

translations.literal: He also had Lü Bu open the tombs of all the emperors and the graves of the Three Excellencies and below, seizing their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Lü Bu to open the imperial tombs and the graves of officials down to the lowest rank, and seize their treasures.

sentences.zh: 卓獲山東兵，以豬膏塗布十餘匹，用纏其身，然後燒之，先從足起。

translations.literal: Zhuo captured eastern soldiers, smeared more than ten bolts of cloth with lard, wrapped their bodies with it, then burned them—the fire starting from the feet.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo captured soldiers from the eastern coalition, he smeared more than ten bolts of cloth with pig fat, wrapped their bodies in the cloth, and set them alight—so that the flames began at their feet.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙巳，車駕入長安，居京兆府捨，後乃稍葺宮室而居之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day yisi, the imperial carriage entered Chang'an and lodged in the Jingzhao prefectural offices; only later were the palace chambers gradually repaired for residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day yisi, the imperial procession entered Chang'an and lodged in the Jingzhao prefectural offices. Only later were the palace halls gradually restored for the court to inhabit.

sentences.zh: 時董卓未至，朝政大小皆委之王允。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Zhuo had not yet arrived; great and small matters of court governance were all entrusted to Wang Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo had not yet arrived, and Wang Yun was entrusted with every matter of government, great and small.

sentences.zh: 允外相彌縫，內謀王室，甚有大臣之度，自天子及朝中皆倚允。

translations.literal: Yun outwardly patched and smoothed relations, inwardly schemed for the royal house—he had very much the measure of a great minister. From the Son of Heaven down through the court, all relied on Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Wang Yun smoothed relations with Dong Zhuo; inwardly he plotted for the house of Han. He bore himself like a true statesman, and from the emperor down the court leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 允屈意承卓，卓亦雅信焉。

translations.literal: Yun bent his will to accommodate Zhuo, and Zhuo also trusted him in refined fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun humbled himself to please Dong Zhuo, and Dong Zhuo in turn placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 董卓以袁紹之故，戊午，殺太傅袁隗、太僕袁基，及其家尺口以上五十餘人。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo, on account of Yuan Shao, on the day wuwu killed Grand Tutor Yuan Wei, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yuan Ji, and more than fifty persons of their households from a foot in height upward.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yuan Shao, on the day wuwu Dong Zhuo executed Grand Tutor Yuan Wei, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yuan Ji, and more than fifty members of their households down to infants a foot tall.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州刺史王睿，與長沙太守孫堅共擊零、桂賊，以堅武官，言頗輕之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Rui, together with Administrator of Changsha Sun Jian, jointly attacked the bandits of Ling and Gui. Because Jian was a military officer, in speech he rather looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Rui, Inspector of Jingzhou, and Sun Jian, Administrator of Changsha, had campaigned together against the bandits of Lingling and Guiyang. Wang Rui looked down on Sun Jian as a mere military man and spoke of him dismissively.

sentences.zh: 及州郡舉兵討董卓，睿與堅亦皆起兵。

translations.literal: When the provinces and commanderies raised troops to attack Dong Zhuo, Rui and Jian also both raised armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the provinces and commanderies rose against Dong Zhuo, Wang Rui and Sun Jian mobilized as well.

sentences.zh: 睿素與武陵太守曹寅不相能，揚言當先殺寅。

translations.literal: Rui had long been unable to get along with Administrator of Wuling Cao Yin and proclaimed that he would first kill Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui had long been at odds with Cao Yin, Administrator of Wuling, and openly declared that he would kill Cao Yin first.

sentences.zh: 寅懼，詐作按行使者檄移堅，說睿罪過，令收，行刑訖，以狀上。

translations.literal: Yin, in fear, forged a dispatch in the name of an investigating commissioner and sent it to Jian, setting forth Rui's crimes and ordering his arrest; after carrying out the punishment, he was to report upward with a statement of the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Cao Yin forged an order in the name of an imperial investigating commissioner and sent it to Sun Jian, listing Wang Rui's crimes and commanding his arrest and execution, with a report to follow once the deed was done.

sentences.zh: 堅承檄，即勒兵襲睿。

translations.literal: Jian received the dispatch and at once led troops to attack Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian accepted the order and immediately marched against Wang Rui.

sentences.zh: 睿聞兵至，登樓望之，遣問：「欲何為？

translations.literal: Rui, hearing troops had come, ascended a tower to look out and sent to ask: "What do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing troops approach, Wang Rui climbed a tower to look out and sent to ask: "What is your purpose?

sentences.zh: 」堅前部答曰：「兵久戰勞苦，欲詣使君求資直耳。

translations.literal: " Jian's vanguard answered: "The troops have fought long and are weary—we wish to come to the Inspector to seek pay and provisions, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Jian's vanguard answered: "The men have fought long and grown weary. We only wish to visit Your Excellency to request pay and supplies.

sentences.zh: 」睿見堅驚曰：「兵自求賞，孫府君何以在其中？

translations.literal: " Rui, seeing Jian, said in alarm: "The troops seek rewards on their own—why is Lord Sun among them?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Rui saw Sun Jian and cried out in alarm: "If the soldiers want their pay, why is Lord Sun himself here?

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「被使者檄誅君！

translations.literal: " Jian said: "I received the commissioner's dispatch to execute you!
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Jian said: "I have been ordered by imperial dispatch to execute you!

sentences.zh: 」睿曰：「我何罪？

translations.literal: " Rui said: "What crime have I committed?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Rui said: "What crime have I committed?

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「坐無所知！

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Your crime is ignorance—failing to know!
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Jian said: "Your crime is ignorance—failing to know what was coming!

sentences.zh: 」睿窮迫，刮金飲之而死。

translations.literal: " Rui, cornered, scraped gold and drank it, then died.
translations.idiomatic: " Driven to bay, Wang Rui scraped gold dust into a cup, drank it, and died.

sentences.zh: 堅前至南陽，眾已數萬人。

translations.literal: Jian advanced to Nanyang; his host already numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian advanced into Nanyang with a force already numbering tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守張咨不肯給軍糧，堅誘而斬之；

translations.literal: Administrator of Nanyang Zhang Zi refused to supply army grain; Jian lured him and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi, Administrator of Nanyang, refused to supply his army with grain. Sun Jian lured him in and executed him;

sentences.zh: 郡中震慄，無求不獲。

translations.literal: the commandery was shaken in awe—no request went unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: and the commandery trembled before him. Nothing he asked for was denied.

sentences.zh: 前到魯陽，與袁術合兵。

translations.literal: Advancing to Luyang, he joined forces with Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on to Luyang and joined forces with Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術由是得據南陽。

translations.literal: Shu thereby came to hold Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu thereby gained control of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 表堅行破虜將軍，領預州刺史。

translations.literal: He memorialized to make Jian acting General Who Smashes the Barbarians, with concurrent charge as Inspector of Yuzhou.
