translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu recommended Sun Jian as acting General Who Smashes the Barbarians and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以北軍中候劉表為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Colonel of the Northern Army Liu Biao Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Liu Biao, Colonel of the Northern Army, Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊縱橫，道路梗塞，表單馬入宜城，請南郡名士蒯良、蒯越與之謀曰：「今江南宗賊甚盛，各擁眾不附，若袁術因之，禍必至矣。

translations.literal: At the time bandits and rebels ran wild and roads were blocked. Biao entered Yicheng alone on horseback, invited the renowned gentlemen of Nan commandery Kuai Liang and Kuai Yue, and plotted with them, saying: "Now the clan-bandits of the south are very strong, each holding hosts and not submitting. If Yuan Shu takes advantage of this, disaster will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits roamed everywhere and the roads were impassable. Liu Biao rode alone into Yicheng and sought counsel from the distinguished men of Nan commandery, Kuai Liang and Kuai Yue. He said: "Clan militias dominate the south, each with its own following and refusing allegiance. If Yuan Shu exploits them, disaster is certain.

sentences.zh: 吾欲徵兵，恐不能集，其策焉出？

translations.literal: I wish to levy troops, but fear I cannot gather them—where should the plan come from?
translations.idiomatic: I wish to raise troops, but I fear I cannot gather them. What is your counsel?

sentences.zh: 」蒯良曰：「眾不附者，仁不足也；

translations.literal: " Kuai Liang said: "Where the multitude does not attach, benevolence is insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: " Kuai Liang said: "When people will not follow you, it is because your benevolence is insufficient;

sentences.zh: 附而不治者，義不足也。

translations.literal: where they attach yet are not governed, righteousness is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: when they follow yet are not well governed, it is because your righteousness is insufficient.

sentences.zh: 苟仁義之道行，百姓歸之如水之趣下，何患徵兵之不集乎？

translations.literal: If the way of benevolence and righteousness is practiced, the common people will return to you like water flowing downward—why worry that levying troops will not gather them?
translations.idiomatic: If benevolence and righteousness truly guide your rule, the people will flock to you as water runs downhill. Why fear that you cannot raise an army?

sentences.zh: 」蒯越曰：「袁術驕而無謀，宗賊帥多貪暴，為下所患，若使人示之以利，必以眾來。

translations.literal: " Kuai Yue said: "Yuan Shu is arrogant and without strategy. The clan-bandit chiefs are mostly greedy and violent, hated by those below them. If we send men to show them profit, they will surely come with their hosts.
translations.idiomatic: " Kuai Yue said: "Yuan Shu is arrogant and shortsighted. Most of the clan chiefs are greedy and brutal, hated by their own followers. Send men to tempt them with gain, and they will bring their bands to you.

sentences.zh: 使君誅其無道，撫而用之，一州之人有樂存之心，聞君威德，必襁負而至矣。

translations.literal: My lord, execute the lawless among them, comfort them and employ them—the people of the province will have hearts glad to endure. Hearing your authority and virtue, they will surely come carrying their infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Execute the worst among them, win over the rest, and the people of the province will rejoice to live under your rule. When they hear of your authority and virtue, they will come carrying their children on their backs.

sentences.zh: 兵集眾附，南據江陵，北守襄陽，荊州八郡可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: With troops gathered and the multitude attached, hold Jiangling in the south and guard Xiangyang in the north—the eight commanderies of Jingzhou can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Once your forces are gathered and the people are with you, hold Jiangling in the south and Xiangyang in the north, and the eight commanderies of Jingzhou can be won by proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 公路雖至，無能為也。

translations.literal: Even if Gonglu arrives, he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yuan Shu comes, he will be powerless.

sentences.zh: 」表曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Biao said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Biao said: "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」乃使越誘宗賊帥，至者五十五人，皆斬之而取其眾。

translations.literal: " He then sent Yue to lure the clan-bandit chiefs; fifty-five came, and all were beheaded and their hosts taken.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Kuai Yue to lure the clan chiefs. Fifty-five came, and he executed them all and absorbed their followers.

sentences.zh: 遂徙治襄陽，鎮撫郡縣，江南悉平。

translations.literal: He then moved his seat of government to Xiangyang, pacified and comforted the commanderies and counties, and the lands south of the Yangzi were all settled.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his seat to Xiangyang, pacified the commanderies and counties, and brought all the lands south of the Yangzi under control.

sentences.zh: 董卓在雒陽，袁紹等諸軍皆畏其強，莫敢先進。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo was in Luoyang; Yuan Shao and the other armies all feared his strength and none dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: While Dong Zhuo held Luoyang, Yuan Shao and the other coalition armies feared his strength and none dared advance.

sentences.zh: 曹操曰：「舉義兵以誅暴亂，大眾已合，諸君何疑！

translations.literal: Cao Cao said: "We have raised righteous troops to punish violent disorder—the great host is already united. Gentlemen, why hesitate!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: "We raised this righteous army to punish tyranny. Our forces are assembled. Why do you hesitate?

sentences.zh: 向使董卓倚王室，據舊京，東向以臨天下，雖以無道行之，猶足為患。

translations.literal: Had Dong Zhuo relied on the royal house, held the old capital, and faced east to overlook all under Heaven—even ruling by the way of lawlessness, he would still have been enough to cause trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If Dong Zhuo had clung to the imperial house, held the old capital, and faced east to dominate the realm, even ruling by brute force he would have been a formidable foe.

sentences.zh: 今焚燒宮室，劫遷天子，海內震動，不知所歸，此天亡之時也，一戰而天下定矣。

translations.literal: Now he burns palace halls, seizes and moves the Son of Heaven—all within the seas is shaken and knows not where to turn. This is the hour when Heaven destroys him; one battle and all under Heaven will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: But he has burned the palaces, seized the emperor, and driven him west. The realm is in uproar and men know not whom to follow. Heaven itself has turned against him. One battle can settle the empire.

sentences.zh: 」遂引兵西，將據成皋，張邈遣將衛茲分兵隨之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led troops west, intending to hold Chenggao. Zhang Miao sent his general Wei Zi with a detachment to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched west toward Chenggao. Zhang Miao sent his general Wei Zi with a detachment to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 進至滎陽汴水，遇卓將玄菟徐榮，與戰，操兵敗，為流矢所中，所乘馬被創。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Bian River at Xingyang, he encountered Zhuo's general Xu Rong of Xuantu and fought. Cao's army was defeated; he was struck by a stray arrow, and the horse he rode was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bian River near Xingyang he met Dong Zhuo's general Xu Rong of Xuantu and gave battle. Cao Cao was defeated, struck by a stray arrow, and his horse was wounded.

sentences.zh: 從弟洪以馬與操，操不受。

translations.literal: His cousin Hong offered his horse to Cao; Cao would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Cao Hong offered him his horse, but Cao Cao refused it.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「天下可無洪，不可無君！

translations.literal: Hong said: "All under Heaven can do without Hong—it cannot do without you, my lord!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong said: "The world can spare me, but it cannot spare you!

sentences.zh: 」遂步從操，夜遁去。

translations.literal: " He thereupon walked on foot following Cao, and in the night they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: " He walked beside Cao Cao on foot, and together they escaped under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 榮見操所將兵少，力戰盡日，謂酸棗未易攻也，亦引兵還。

translations.literal: Rong, seeing how few troops Cao commanded and that he had fought fiercely all day, said Suanzao would not be easy to attack and also withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong saw how few men Cao Cao had led and how fiercely they had fought all day. Judging that the coalition camp at Suanzao would not be easy to take, he withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 操到酸棗，諸軍十餘萬，日置酒高會，不圖進取，操責讓之，因為謀曰：「諸君□能聽吾計，使渤海引河內之眾臨孟津，酸棗諸將守成皋，據敖倉，塞轘轅、太谷，全制其險，使袁將軍率南陽之軍軍丹、析，入武關，以震三輔，皆高壘深壁，勿與戰，益為疑兵，示天下形勢，以順誅逆，可立定也。

translations.literal: Cao reached Suanzao. The various armies numbered more than a hundred thousand; day after day they set out wine and held high feasts, not planning to advance. Cao reproached and blamed them, and on that account offered a plan, saying: "If you gentlemen can heed my plan, let Bohai lead the forces of Henei to press on Mengjin; the generals at Suanzao hold Chenggao, occupy Aocang, block Huanyuan and Taigu, fully control the strategic passes; let General Yuan lead the troops of Nanyang to encamp at Dan and Xi, enter Wu Pass to shake the Three Adjuncts—all building high ramparts and deep walls, not giving battle, increasing deceptive troops, displaying the posture of all under Heaven, and with legitimacy punishing rebellion—all can be settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao reached Suanzao, he found more than a hundred thousand coalition troops feasting day after day with no thought of advancing. He rebuked them and laid out a plan: "If you gentlemen can heed my plan, let Yuan Shao of Bohai bring the forces of Henei against Mengjin. The generals at Suanzao should hold Chenggao, occupy Aocang, and seal Huanyuan and Taigu, controlling every strategic pass. Let General Yuan Shu lead the Nanyang army to camp at Dan and Xi and enter Wu Pass to threaten the Three Adjuncts. Build high walls and deep trenches everywhere, avoid battle, multiply deceptive displays, and show the realm our united strength. With legitimacy on our side and rebellion before us, the empire can be settled at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 今兵以義動，持疑不進，失天下望，竊為諸君恥之！

translations.literal: Now the army moves on righteousness, yet holds back in doubt and does not advance—you lose the hope of all under Heaven. I privately feel shame for you gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: You raised this army in the name of righteousness, yet you hang back in doubt. You are squandering the hopes of the realm—and I am ashamed for you!

sentences.zh: 」邈等不能用。

translations.literal: " Miao and the others could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Miao and the others would not adopt his plan.

sentences.zh: 操乃與司馬沛國夏侯惇等詣揚州募兵，得千餘人，還屯河內。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon, with Major Xiahou Dun of Pei and others, went to Yang province to levy troops, obtained a little more than a thousand men, and returned to garrison Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then went with his major Xiahou Dun of Pei and others to Yang province to raise troops. He gathered a little more than a thousand men and returned to camp at Henei.

sentences.zh: 頃之，酸棗諸軍食盡，眾散。

translations.literal: Before long, the armies at Suanzao exhausted their food and the hosts dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the coalition armies at Suanzao ran out of provisions and scattered.

sentences.zh: 劉岱與橋瑁相惡，岱殺瑁，以王肱領東郡太守。

translations.literal: Liu Dai and Qiao Mao bore ill will toward each other; Dai killed Mao and made Wang Gong act as Administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai and Qiao Mao hated each other. Liu Dai killed Qiao Mao and installed Wang Gong as Administrator of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史焦和亦起兵討董卓，務及諸將西行，不為民人保障，兵始濟河，黃巾已入其境。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qingzhou Jiao He also raised troops to attack Dong Zhuo. Intent on joining the generals marching west, he gave the common people no protection. His troops had only just crossed the river when the Yellow Turbans had already entered his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao He, Inspector of Qingzhou, also raised troops against Dong Zhuo. Eager to join the western campaign, he left the people undefended. His army had barely crossed the Yellow River when the Yellow Turbans were already inside his province.

sentences.zh: 青州素殷實，甲兵甚盛，和每望寇奔北，未嘗接風塵、交旗鼓也。

translations.literal: Qingzhou had long been wealthy and substantial, with armor and weapons very strong—but He, whenever he saw the bandits, fled north. He never once met the dust of battle or crossed banners and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou had long been prosperous and well armed, yet whenever Jiao He sighted the enemy he fled north. He never once met them in battle.

sentences.zh: 性好卜筮，信鬼神。

translations.literal: His nature delighted in divination and he trusted in ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in divination and trusted in ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 入見其人，清談干雲，出觀其政，賞罰淆亂，州遂蕭條，悉為丘墟。

translations.literal: Entering to see the man, one found lofty discourse reaching to the clouds; going out to observe his government, rewards and punishments were confused and disorderly—the province grew desolate and all became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: In person he offered lofty discourse reaching to the clouds; in government his rewards and punishments were confused and disorderly—the province grew desolate until all lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 頃之，和病卒，袁紹使廣陵臧洪領青州以撫之。

translations.literal: Before long He died of illness; Yuan Shao had Zang Hong of Guangling take charge of Qing Province to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long He died of illness; Yuan Shao had Zang Hong of Guangling take charge of Qing Province to pacify it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以幽州牧劉虞為太傅，道路壅塞，信命竟不得通。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Liu Yu, Governor of You Province, was made Grand Tutor, but the roads were blocked and his commission and orders could not get through in the end.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Liu Yu, Governor of You Province, was appointed Grand Tutor, but the roads were blocked and his commission never reached him.

sentences.zh: 先是，幽部應接荒外，資費甚廣，歲常割青、冀賦調二億有餘以足之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the You region had to meet the needs of the outer wilds and its expenses were very great; each year more than two hundred million from the tax levies of Qing and Ji was cut off to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the You region had to meet the needs of the outer frontier and its expenses were very great; each year more than two hundred million from the tax levies of Qing and Ji was diverted to supply it.

sentences.zh: 時處處斷絕，委輸不至，而虞敝衣繩屨，食無兼肉，務存寬政，勸督農桑，開上谷胡市之利，通漁陽鹽鐵之饒，民悅年登，谷石三十，青、徐士庶避難歸虞者百餘萬口，虞皆收視溫恤，為安立生業，流民皆忘其遷徙焉。

translations.literal: At that time communications were cut off everywhere and deliveries did not arrive, yet Yu wore worn clothes and rope sandals, ate no second meat dish, devoted himself to lenient government, urged and supervised farming and sericulture, opened the profits of the Hu markets in Shanggu, and linked the abundance of Yuyang's salt and iron; the people were pleased, harvests were good, and grain was thirty cash per picul. More than a million people from Qing and Xu who fled calamity came to Yu; he received, cared for, and warmed them all, settled them in livelihoods, and the displaced forgot they had ever moved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time communications were cut off everywhere and supplies did not arrive, yet Yu wore worn clothes and rope sandals, ate no second meat dish, devoted himself to lenient government, urged farming and sericulture, opened the profits of the Hu markets in Shanggu, and tapped the abundance of Yuyang's salt and iron; the people were pleased, harvests were good, and grain sold for thirty cash per picul. More than a million people from Qing and Xu who fled calamity came to Yu; he received and cared for them all, settled them in livelihoods, and the displaced forgot they had ever been uprooted.

sentences.zh: 五月，司空荀爽薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Minister of Works Xun Shuang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Minister of Works Xun Shuang died.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛丑，以光祿大夫種拂為司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinchou, Palace Counsellor Zhong Fu was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinchou day, Palace Counsellor Zhong Fu was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 拂，邵之父也。

translations.literal: Fu was the father of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was the father of Shao.

sentences.zh: 董卓遣大鴻臚韓融、少府陰修、執金吾胡毋班、將作大匠吳修、越騎校尉王瑰安集關東，解譬袁紹等。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo sent the Grand Herald Han Rong, the Minister Steward Yin Xiu, the Bearer of the Mace Huwuban, the Master of Works Wu Xiu, and the Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Wang Gui to pacify and gather the east of the passes and to explain and persuade Yuan Shao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent Grand Herald Han Rong, Minister Steward Yin Xiu, Bearer of the Mace Huwuban, Master of Works Wu Xiu, and Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Wang Gui to pacify the east of the passes and persuade Yuan Shao and the others.

sentences.zh: 胡毋班、吳修、王瑰至河內，袁紹使王匡悉收系殺之。

translations.literal: Huwuban, Wu Xiu, and Wang Gui reached Henei; Yuan Shao had Wang Kuang seize and kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Huwuban, Wu Xiu, and Wang Gui reached Henei; Yuan Shao had Wang Kuang seize and kill them all.

sentences.zh: 袁術亦殺陰修，惟韓融以名德免。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu also killed Yin Xiu; only Han Rong was spared because of his fame and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu also killed Yin Xiu; only Han Rong was spared because of his fame and virtue.

sentences.zh: 董卓壞五銖錢，更鑄小錢，悉取雒陽及長安銅人、鐘虡、飛廉、銅馬之屬以鑄之，由是貨賤物貴，谷石至數萬錢。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo destroyed the five-zhu coins and cast small coins instead, taking all the bronze men, bell stands, Flying Bronzes, bronze horses, and the like of Luoyang and Chang'an to cast them; from this money grew cheap and goods dear, and grain reached tens of thousands of cash per picul.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo destroyed the five-zhu coins and cast small coins instead, melting down the bronze men, bell stands, Flying Bronzes, bronze horses, and the like of Luoyang and Chang'an to cast them; from this money grew cheap and goods dear, and grain reached tens of thousands of cash per picul.

sentences.zh: 冬，孫堅與官屬會飲於魯陽城東，董卓步騎數萬猝至，堅方行酒談笑，整頓部曲，無得妄動。

translations.literal: In winter, Sun Jian was drinking with his officials east of Luyang city when several tens of thousands of Dong Zhuo's infantry and cavalry arrived suddenly; Jian was just passing wine and talking and laughing, yet he put his troops in order and forbade any rash movement.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Sun Jian was drinking with his officials east of Luyang when several tens of thousands of Dong Zhuo's infantry and cavalry arrived suddenly; Jian was still passing wine and talking and laughing, yet he put his troops in order and forbade any rash movement.

sentences.zh: 後騎漸益，堅徐罷坐，導引入城，乃曰：「向堅所以不即起走，恐兵相蹈藉，諸君不得入耳。

translations.literal: The rear cavalry gradually increased; Jian slowly ended the feast and led them into the city, then said: "The reason I did not rise and flee at once was that I feared the troops would trample one another and you gentlemen would not get inside the city."
translations.idiomatic: The rear cavalry gradually increased; Jian slowly ended the feast and led them into the city, then said: "The reason I did not flee at once was that I feared the troops would trample one another and you gentlemen would not get inside the walls."

sentences.zh: 」卓兵見其整，不敢攻而還。

translations.literal: Zhuo's troops saw how orderly they were, did not dare attack, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's troops saw how orderly they were, did not dare attack, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王匡屯河陽津，董卓襲擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Wang Kuang encamped at Heyang Ford; Dong Zhuo attacked by surprise and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang encamped at Heyang Ford; Dong Zhuo attacked by surprise and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 左中郎將蔡邕議：「孝和以下廟號稱宗者，皆宜省去，以遵先典。

translations.literal: The General of the Left Zhonglang Cai Yong proposed: "For temple names below Emperor Xiaohe that use the title 'Zong,' all ought to be omitted to follow the ancient canon."
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Zhonglang Cai Yong proposed: "For temple names below Emperor Xiaohe that use the title 'Zong,' all ought to be omitted to follow the ancient canon."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 中郎將徐榮薦同郡故冀州刺史公孫度於董卓，卓以為遼東太守。

translations.literal: The General of the Zhonglang Xu Rong recommended to Dong Zhuo his fellow townsman, the former Governor of Ji Province Gongsun Du; Zhuo made him Administrator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Zhonglang Xu Rong recommended to Dong Zhuo his fellow townsman, former Governor of Ji Province Gongsun Du; Zhuo appointed him Administrator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 度到官，以法誅滅郡中名豪大姓百餘家，郡中震慄，乃東伐高句驪，西擊烏桓，語所親吏柳毅、陽儀等曰：「漢祚將絕，當與諸卿圖王耳。

translations.literal: When Du reached his post, he executed by law more than a hundred great clans and eminent houses of the commandery; the commandery trembled in fear. He then campaigned east against Gaogouli and struck west at the Wuhuan, and said to his intimate officials Liu Yi, Yang Yi, and the others: "The fortune of Han is about to end—we ought to plot kingship together, you and I."
translations.idiomatic: When Du reached his post, he executed by law more than a hundred great clans and eminent houses of the commandery; the commandery trembled in fear. He then campaigned east against Gaogouli and struck west at the Wuhuan, and said to his intimate officials Liu Yi, Yang Yi, and the others: "The fortune of Han is about to end—we ought to plot kingship together."

sentences.zh: 」於是分遼東為遼西、中遼郡，各置太守，越海收東萊諸縣，置營州刺史。

translations.literal: He thereupon divided Liaodong into the commanderies of Liaoxi and Zhongliao, setting an administrator in each; crossed the sea to take the counties of Donglai and established a Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon divided Liaodong into the commanderies of Liaoxi and Zhongliao, appointing an administrator in each; crossed the sea to take the counties of Donglai and established a Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 自立為遼東侯、平州牧，立漢二祖廟，承製，郊祀天地，藉田，乘鸞路，設旄頭、羽騎。

translations.literal: He set himself up as Marquis of Liaodong and Governor of Ping Province, established temples to the two Han ancestors, assumed imperial regulations, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, performed the ceremonial plowing, rode the imperial carriage with phoenix bells, and established the Mao Tou and Feather Cavalry guards.
translations.idiomatic: He set himself up as Marquis of Liaodong and Governor of Ping Province, established temples to the two Han ancestors, assumed imperial regulations, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, performed the ceremonial plowing, rode the imperial carriage with phoenix bells, and established the Mao Tou and Feather Cavalry guards.
